This sensor can be tuned to target a specific resource type. It consumes a lot of electricity. If you find a resource, you'll need to travel to collect it.

ThingDef.label: pod launcher
ThingDef.description: A fueling port for launching one transport pod. Pod launchers can launch as a group - but the launchers must be placed adjacent to each other.

ThingDef.label: transport pod
ThingDef.description: A launchable sub-orbital cargo pod capable of carrying people, items, or animals. Can be used for sending gifts, transporting people or supplies, surprise attacks, or reinforcing battles.

ThingDef.label: multi-analyzer
ThingDef.description: Increases research speed when placed near hi-tech research bench and unlocks new research projects. Each research bench can only use one multi-analyzer.

ThingDef.label: vitals monitor
ThingDef.description: Increases medical tend quality, surgery success chance, and immunity gain speed when placed directly adjacent to a hospital bed. Only works for hospital beds - normal beds will not benefit. Attaching more than one vitals monitor to the same bed will have no effect.

ThingDef.label: tool cabinet
ThingDef.description: Increases work speed when placed near a workbench. One workbench can use up to two tool cabinets.

ThingDef.label: grave
ThingDef.description: A decent final resting place. Colonists will visit full graves to gain meditative joy.

ThingDef.label: sarcophagus
ThingDef.description: An ornamented burial receptacle for the honored dead.

ThingDef.label: cryptosleep casket
ThingDef.description: A self-powered sarcophagus designed to keep a person in a state of suspended animation for many years.

ThingDef.Name: AncientCryptosleepCasket
ThingDef.label: ancient cryptosleep casket
ThingDef.description: This cryptosleep casket looks like it has been here for a very long time. Who knows what it might contain?

ThingDef.label: marriage spot
ThingDef.description: Designates a spot where marriage ceremonies will take place. Spectators can watch from either side.

ThingDef.label: party spot
ThingDef.description: Designates a spot for throwing parties.

ThingDef.label: caravan hitching spot
ThingDef.description: Designates a spot for hitching animals and forming caravans. Colonists will hitch animals here while loading a caravan. You can also use these during encounters away from home to keep animals from wandering.

ThingDef.label: large stele
ThingDef.description: A tall, thick slab with engravings on the sides. Steles have been used since ancient times to memorialize individuals, battles, and other important events.

ThingDef.label: grand stele
ThingDef.description: A towering slab with extensive engravings on the sides. Steles have been used since ancient times to memorialize individuals, battles, and other important events.

ThingDef.label: pen marker
ThingDef.description: A post with a sign designating an animal pen. It must be placed in an area enclosed by fences, barricades, walls, and doors. You can assign each pen marker a set of animals to accept, and handlers will bring animals to an appropriate pen.

ThingDef.label: unfinished musical instrument
ThingDef.description: An unfinished musical instrument.

ThingDef.label: collapsed rocks
ThingDef.description: Collapsed rocks, packed tightly enough to hold up a roof.

ThingDef.label: compacted steel
ThingDef.description: The remains of some ancient, collapsed structure. Rich in steel.

ThingDef.label: silver ore
ThingDef.description: Rock containing bits of silver.

ThingDef.label: gold ore
ThingDef.description: Rock containing bits of gold.

ThingDef.label: uranium ore
ThingDef.description: Rock containing bits of uranium.

ThingDef.label: compacted plasteel
ThingDef.description: Ancient compacted rubble rich in plasteel.

ThingDef.label: jade
ThingDef.description: Rock containing bits of jade.

ThingDef.label: compacted machinery
ThingDef.description: Ancient machinery, compacted over time. Can be mined for useful components.

ThingDef.label: steam geyser
ThingDef.description: A natural source of high-pressure steam. Geothermal generators can harness the steam power. Rooms built over this will rapidly cook.

ThingDef.label: hive
ThingDef.description: A hive of giant insects. If activated, it will spawn additional insects and hives over time, as well as valuable insect jelly.

ThingDef.label: glow pod
ThingDef.description: A bioluminescent pod produced by giant insects. Glows under its own light for a long time, then dies.

ThingDef.Name: RaisedRocks
ThingDef.label: raised rocks
ThingDef.description: A fragile wall made of rubble. It will collapse in time.

ThingDef.Name: PowerConduit
ThingDef.label: power conduit
ThingDef.description: A bundle of electrical cables for moving power around. Can be placed under walls and other buildings.

ThingDef.label: hidden conduit
ThingDef.description: Hidden electrical cables for moving power around. They're tougher than regular conduits, but also slower to build and more expensive.

ThingDef.label: waterproof conduit
ThingDef.description: Insulated electrical cables for transmitting power under shallow water.

ThingDef.label: power switch
ThingDef.description: Switches power on/off.

ThingDef.label: wood-fired generator
ThingDef.description: Produces power by consuming wood. Must be periodically loaded with wood fuel by hand.

ThingDef.label: chemfuel powered generator
ThingDef.description: Produces power by consuming chemfuel. Must be periodically refueled by hand.

ThingDef.label: wind turbine
ThingDef.description: A wind-powered electrical generator. Requires a large clear space in front and behind for optimal air flow.

ThingDef.label: battery
ThingDef.description: Stores electricity for later use. Charged batteries explode when exposed to rain or fire.

ThingDef.label: solar generator
ThingDef.description: Produces electricity from sunlight. Does not work in the dark or under artificial light.

ThingDef.label: geothermal generator
ThingDef.description: Produces electricity from geothermal steam geysers. Must be placed on a steam geyser.

ThingDef.label: watermill generator
ThingDef.description: Produces electricity from a river. Must be placed with its wheel in moving water. If watermills are placed too close together, the turbulence they generate will interfere and reduce power generation.

ThingDef.label: crafting spot
ThingDef.description: A place for crafting simple items like knives or bows. Production here is slow because of the lack of tools.

ThingDef.label: butcher spot
ThingDef.description: A place for butchering animals. Due to the lack of equipment, butchering here yields only 70% of the meat and leather of each creature.

ThingDef.label: art bench
ThingDef.description: A workbench equipped for creating art.

ThingDef.label: butcher table
ThingDef.description: A heavy table for butchering dead creatures into pieces of raw meat. Rotting or dessicated corpses cannot be butchered.

ThingDef.label: hand tailor bench
ThingDef.description: A workbench for tailoring clothes by hand. Works at 50% of the speed of an electric tailoring bench.

ThingDef.label: electric tailor bench
ThingDef.description: A workbench with a sewing machine for rapid tailoring of clothes. Can work without electricity at 50% of normal speed.

ThingDef.label: fueled smithy
ThingDef.description: A wood-fueled station for smithing non-mechanical weapons and tools.

ThingDef.label: electric smithy
ThingDef.description: An electric-powered station for smithing non-mechanical weapons and tools.

ThingDef.label: machining table
ThingDef.description: A work station for assembling machinery like guns and ammunition, or breaking down dead mechanoids.

ThingDef.label: electric stove
ThingDef.description: An electrically-powered stove with an attached countertop for preparing meals.

ThingDef.label: fueled stove
ThingDef.description: A wood-fueled stove with an attached countertop for preparing meals.

ThingDef.label: stonecutter's table
ThingDef.description: A work table with saws and chisels for cutting stone chunks into usable blocks.

ThingDef.label: brewery
ThingDef.description: A work station with all the equipment needed to mix wort for beer production. Wort must be fermented to finally become beer.

ThingDef.label: drug lab
ThingDef.description: A work bench equipped with containers, heaters, and measurement devices for producing various drugs.

ThingDef.label: electric smelter
ThingDef.description: Extracts usable metal from slag chunks and other mixed metal items. Consumes a lot of power.

ThingDef.label: biofuel refinery
ThingDef.description: Refines biological matter like wood or plant matter into chemfuel.

ThingDef.label: fabrication bench
ThingDef.description: A workbench equipped with advanced tools for producing technological marvels from simpler materials.

ThingDef.label: simple research bench
ThingDef.description: A simple bench with writing implements and simple measurement devices. Researchers work here to discover new things.

ThingDef.label: hi-tech research bench
ThingDef.description: A high-tech bench with computers and electronic measurement equipment. Allows more rapid research, and unlocks advanced research projects.

ThingDef.label: electric crematorium
ThingDef.description: A huge stone crematorium which vaporizes corpses with extremely high temperatures.

ThingDef.label: hydroponics basin
ThingDef.description: An artificial nutrient bath for growing plants. The nutrients pumps must work continuously; the plants will die if power is cut.

ThingDef.label: fermenting barrel
ThingDef.description: A barrel for fermenting raw wort into beer.

ThingDef.label: deep drill
ThingDef.description: A deep-crust drilling rig for extracting minerals from deep under the surface. Use a ground-penetrating scanner to detect the resources. This drill will yield stone chunks if no resources are present. Can be repositioned freely.

ThingDef.label: nutrient paste dispenser
ThingDef.description: A machine that synthesizes edible nutrient paste from organic feedstocks placed in adjacent hoppers. It consumes less ingredients and time than any other meal production method - but nobody likes eating nutrient paste. Accepts raw food, but not rough plant matter like hay.

ThingDef.label: hopper
ThingDef.description: Holds resources for use by machines like nutrient paste dispensers.

ThingDef.label: sandbags
ThingDef.description: Bags of locally-sourced dirt or sand, stacked for use as cover. Sandbags are ugly, but provide better cover than other low objects.

ThingDef.label: barricade
ThingDef.description: A waist-high barrier for use as cover from incoming shots. Barricades are ugly, but provide better cover than other low objects. Barricades will block certain kinds of animals the same way that fences do.

ThingDef.label: spike trap
ThingDef.description: Five spikes under tension, connected to a touch-activated trigger. When the victim disturbs the trigger, the spikes spring forth and strike the victim. Since it is hidden in the surrounding terrain, it cannot be placed adjacent to other traps. Animals can sense these when calm.

ThingDef.label: IED trap
ThingDef.description: A pair of high-explosive shells connected to a trigger which detonates on touch or bullet impact. Since it is hidden in the surrounding terrain, it cannot be placed adjacent to other traps. Animals can sense these when calm.

ThingDef.label: IED incendiary trap
ThingDef.description: A pair of incendiary shells connected to a trigger which detonates on touch or bullet impact. Since it is hidden in the surrounding terrain, it cannot be placed adjacent to other traps. Animals can sense these when calm.

ThingDef.label: IED EMP trap
ThingDef.description: A pair of EMP shells connected to a trigger which detonates on touch or bullet impact. The explosion can paralyze mechanoids for a few seconds. Since it is hidden in the surrounding terrain, it cannot be placed adjacent to other traps. Animals can sense these when calm.

ThingDef.label: IED smoke trap
ThingDef.description: A pair of smoke shells connected to a trigger which detonates on touch or bullet impact. Since it is hidden in the surrounding terrain, it cannot be placed adjacent to other traps. Animals can sense these when calm.

ThingDef.label: IED firefoam trap
ThingDef.description: A pair of firefoam shells connected to a trigger which detonates on touch or bullet impact. Since it is hidden in the surrounding terrain, it cannot be placed adjacent to other traps. Animals can sense these when calm.

ThingDef.label: IED antigrain warhead trap
ThingDef.description: An antimatter-powered antigrain warhead connected to a trigger which detonates on touch or bullet impact. Since it is hidden in the surrounding terrain, it cannot be placed adjacent to other traps. Animals can sense these when calm.

ThingDef.label: mini-turret
ThingDef.description: A portable automatic turret. Requires steel to refurbish its barrel after heavy use. May explode when damaged. Its dumb AI brain can't be directly controlled, so beware of friendly fire.

ThingDef.label: mini-turret gun
ThingDef.description: A simple automatic gun made to be mounted on a turret.

ThingDef.label: autocannon turret
ThingDef.description: A heavy automatic turret. Its large-caliber shells do heavy damage over significant ranges, but its barrel must be refurbished after use. It cannot fire at close-up targets, and may explode when damaged.

ThingDef.label: autocannon
ThingDef.description: A self-loading large-bore cannon designed to attach to a turret.

ThingDef.label: uranium slug turret
ThingDef.description: An armor-piercing turret. Its ultra-dense uranium shells can punch through heavy armor, but it requires new uranium slugs to be loaded after use. It's more accurate at longer ranges, and can't fire at all close up. May explode when damaged.

ThingDef.label: uranium slug cannon
ThingDef.description: A self-loading uranium slug cannon designed to attach to a turret.

ThingDef.label: mortar
ThingDef.description: A manned mortar that launches all kinds of shells. While it can inflict devastating damage, the mortar's inherent inaccuracy makes it more useful for attacking large fortifications than groups of enemies in the field.

ThingDef.label: mortar
ThingDef.description: Mortar launcher. Lobs bombs over walls. Very inaccurate but long-ranged.

ThingDef.label: foam turret
ThingDef.description: An activatable turret for extinguishing fires. The turret stands idle until someone approaches and activates it, after which it will automatically spray large amounts of firefoam on any flames in sight.

ThingDef.label: foam sprayer
ThingDef.description: A high-pressure firefoam sprayer usually mounted on a turret.

ThingDef.label: rocketswarm launcher
ThingDef.description: An emergency-defense launcher that fires a single barrage of rockets covering a large area. The turret does not fire until someone activates it. It is very effective against large groups of weaker combatants, but less effective against small numbers of armored targets. Once fired, it must cool off for hours and be reloaded to fire again.

ThingDef.label: rocketswarm tube
ThingDef.description: A rocketswarm tube of the type usually mounted on a rocketswarm launcher turret.

ThingDef.label: ship structural beam
ThingDef.description: A structural beam around which a starship can be constructed. Includes all the necessary conduits and transit pipes for communications, power, and materials transport.

ThingDef.label: ship cryptosleep casket
ThingDef.description: A cryptosleep casket hardened against the dangers of space. Capable of maintaining a person in cryptosleep for centuries and surviving atmospheric re-entry.

ThingDef.label: ship computer core
ThingDef.description: A computer core housing a machine persona who can guide a starship through any challenge during a multi-decade starflight.

ThingDef.label: ship reactor
ThingDef.description: Powers a ship on its journey between stars. Takeoff requires a long powerup process that is likely to attract raiders.

ThingDef.label: ship engine
ThingDef.description: A reactionless Johnson-Tanaka drive capable of launching a ship into orbit, and crawling across the vast expanses between stars.

ThingDef.label: sensor cluster
ThingDef.description: A multi-function sensor module. Can scan and signal across the void for communications, threat detection, deception, jamming, and other purposes.

ThingDef.label: psychic emanator
ThingDef.description: An ancient device that projects a soothing psychic field around itself. This improves the mood of anyone nearby. Works through walls.

ThingDef.label: vanometric power cell
ThingDef.description: Generates free energy, forever, without using fuel. This technology is developed by archotechs, and is beyond even most glitterworld societies. While nobody knows exactly how it works, scholars believe it somehow extracts energy directly from fluctuations in the quantum foam.

ThingDef.label: infinite chemreactor
ThingDef.description: Slowly generates chemfuel by a complex series of chemical reactions, using atoms extracted from the air.

ThingDef.Name: Door
ThingDef.label: door
ThingDef.description: Divides rooms. Simple doors must be manually opened, which slows people down. The amount of slowdown depends on what the door is made of.

ThingDef.label: autodoor
ThingDef.description: Divides rooms. Powered operation allows people to move through the door without slowing down.

ThingDef.label: animal flap
ThingDef.description: A doorway hung with thick overlapping strips of fabric or leather. It allows animals to pass while insulating the temperature. Animal flaps are commonly used as barn doors to give penned animals a sheltered place to sleep.

ThingDef.label: ornate door
ThingDef.description: Divides rooms. An intricately-carved door, decorated with gold. This large, heavy door requires adjacent walls to function.

ThingDef.Name: Wall
ThingDef.label: wall
ThingDef.description: An impassable wall. Capable of holding up a roof.

ThingDef.label: fence
ThingDef.description: A fence made of posts joined by crossbars used for building pens for certain kinds of animals. Some kinds of animals can get past fences. Predators will not hunt creatures on the other side of a fence, but may still wander inside.

ThingDef.label: fence gate
ThingDef.description: A simple gate made of posts and crossbars. It blocks some animals like a fence. Handlers can lead animals in and out of the pen through these gates.

ThingDef.label: column
ThingDef.description: A column capable of holding a roof. Does not block sight or movement and looks quite nice.

ThingDef.label: campfire
ThingDef.description: Cooks meals and produces heat, and burns out after a few days. As with all heat sources, it must be placed indoors so it has a closed space to heat. Refuelable.

ThingDef.label: passive cooler
ThingDef.description: A traditional unpowered cooler that works by water evaporation. Must be regularly replenished with wood. Not efficient enough to refrigerate food.

ThingDef.label: heater
ThingDef.description: A device that converts electricity into heat. It can automatically turn itself on or off to reach a specific target temperature.

ThingDef.Name: Cooler
ThingDef.label: cooler
ThingDef.description: An air-cooling machine that fits into a wall. Cool air comes out one side, while hot exhaust comes out the other. Can be used to cool down rooms during summer, or to create a walk-in freezer.

ThingDef.Name: Vent
ThingDef.label: vent
ThingDef.description: A vent for equalizing the temperature between two rooms without allowing people to walk between them.

ThingDef.label: psychic animal pulser
ThingDef.description: A one-use broad-wave psychic effector. The psychic pulse fills lower minds with terrifying imagery, driving all animals in the region into a manhunting rage. Animals currently under your control will not be affected.

ThingDef.label: psychic soothe pulser
ThingDef.description: A one-use broad-wave psychic effector. The psychic pulse induces self-satisfying perceptual distortions, giving a temporary mood boost to everyone in the region.

ThingDef.label: persona core
ThingDef.description: A hyper-advanced computer core that houses a peak-human-equivalent machine persona. In its isolated state, the core is dormant. Installed in a proper support structure, however, it can become a mind of great power.

ThingDef.label: healer mech serum
ThingDef.description: A one-use super-dose of mechanites tuned to heal health conditions. The mechanites will target and heal the single worst health condition affecting someone at any given time. Works even on health conditions that would otherwise be incurable. The mechanites can even transmute themselves into organic matter, forming new limbs or organs as needed.

ThingDef.label: resurrector mech serum
ThingDef.description: A one-use super-dose of mechanites tuned to resurrect the dead. Administered to a corpse, mechanites repair broken-down tissues and kickstart the body back to life. Unfortunately, the resurrected sometimes come back with brain damage, blindness, or progressive psychosis. Outcomes are better when the mechanites are administered to a fresher body. If a body is preserved, it can even be resurrected long after death.\n\nThe resurrected also experience limited retrograde amnesia, forgetting some recent memories and social interactions.

ThingDef.label: techprof subpersona core
ThingDef.description: A small AI core housing a low-grade subpersona specialized in teaching technology. When used, the AI will teach you the technology you're currently researching, instantly and for free. Can only be used once.

ThingDef.label: thrumbo horn
ThingDef.description: A thrumbo's horn. It's razor-sharp, rock-hard, and priceless in most markets. This is a true trophy, as well as a deadly melee weapon.

ThingDef.label: elephant tusk
ThingDef.description: An elephant's tusk. It is very durable and valuable. While somewhat unwieldy as a melee weapon, it can still be deadly.

ThingDef.label: packaged survival meal
ThingDef.description: A high-quality packaged meal, manufactured for use in survival situations. While it never rots, it can still deteriorate if left outside. Great for traveling.

ThingDef.label: nutrient paste meal
ThingDef.description: A synthetic mixture of protein, carbohydrates, and vitamins, amino acids and minerals. Everything the body needs, and absolutely disgusting.

ThingDef.label: simple meal
ThingDef.description: A simple meal quickly cooked from one main ingredient.

ThingDef.label: fine meal
ThingDef.description: A complex dish assembled with care from a variety of ingredients.

ThingDef.label: vegetarian fine meal
ThingDef.description: A complex dish assembled with care from vegetarian ingredients.

ThingDef.label: carnivore fine meal
ThingDef.description: A complex dish assembled with care from meat ingredients.

ThingDef.Name: MealLavishBase
ThingDef.description: A masterpiece of the culinary arts, this meal nourishes the body, mind, and soul.

ThingDef.label: kibble
ThingDef.description: Animal feed made from mixed meat and plant sources. Humans can eat it, but they really, really don't like it.

ThingDef.label: pemmican
ThingDef.description: A preserved mashed mixture of fat and plant food. Tastes bland, but not offensive. It lasts a very long time without refrigeration. Great for traveling.

ThingDef.label: chocolate
ThingDef.description: A delicious preparation of cocoa seeds ground together with sugar and vanilla. It fulfills the need for recreation, but it is not very nutritious.

ThingDef.label: milk
ThingDef.description: Milk from an animal.\n\nMilk can be fed to human babies.

ThingDef.label: insect jelly
ThingDef.description: Jelly stored and used as food by oversized insects. It is smooth, rich, and fulfills the recreation need of those who consume it. Because of its unique biological properties, it can nourish almost any creature and never rots.\n\nOddly, its texture and nutrient balance makes it an ideal baby food.

ThingDef.label: skull
ThingDef.description: A human skull.

ThingDef.label: chicken egg (unfert.)
ThingDef.description: An unfertilized chicken egg. It can be eaten raw, but it's much, much better cooked.

ThingDef.label: chicken egg (fert.)
ThingDef.description: A fertilized chicken egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a chick. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.

ThingDef.label: cobra egg (fert.)
ThingDef.description: A fertilized cobra egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby cobra. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.

ThingDef.label: iguana egg (fert.)
ThingDef.description: A fertilized iguana egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby iguana. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.

ThingDef.label: tortoise egg (fert.)
ThingDef.description: A fertilized tortoise egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby tortoise. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.

ThingDef.label: cassowary egg (fert.)
ThingDef.description: A fertilized cassowary egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby cassowary. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.

ThingDef.label: emu egg (fert.)
ThingDef.description: A fertilized emu egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby emu. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.

ThingDef.label: ostrich egg (fert.)
ThingDef.description: A fertilized ostrich egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby ostrich. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.

ThingDef.label: turkey egg (fert.)
ThingDef.description: A fertilized turkey egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby turkey. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.

ThingDef.label: duck egg (unfert.)
ThingDef.description: An unfertilized duck egg. It can be eaten raw, but it's much, much better cooked.

ThingDef.label: duck egg (fert.)
ThingDef.description: A fertilized duck egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a duckling. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.

ThingDef.label: goose egg (unfert.)
ThingDef.description: An unfertilized goose egg. It can be eaten raw, but it's much, much better cooked.

ThingDef.label: goose egg (fert.)
ThingDef.description: A fertilized goose egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby goose. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.

ThingDef.label: herbal medicine
ThingDef.description: A pack of herbal concoctions extracted from the healroot plant. It is less potent than industrial pharmaceuticals, but much better than nothing.

ThingDef.label: medicine
ThingDef.description: A kit of industrial-era medical equipment. It contains basic drugs, tools for suturing and bone setting, diagnostic devices, and various pads and fluids.

ThingDef.label: glitterworld medicine
ThingDef.description: A kit of advanced ultra-tech medical supplies, probably manufactured on a distant glitterworld. It contains advanced polymorphic drugs, nanite diagnostic and healing assisters, a mini-imager, and various multi-use tools.

ThingDef.label: component
ThingDef.description: Miscellaneous gears, capacitors, circuit boards, tubes, wheels, sensors, wires, chips, processors, and other electronic and industrial parts. Necessary for assembling complex machines or electronics.

ThingDef.label: advanced component
ThingDef.description: Advanced computing and energy-directing machinery, miniaturized and hardened for the most demanding applications.

ThingDef.label: neutroamine
ThingDef.description: A synthetic precursor chemical. While it is useless on its own, many drugs require neutroamine as an ingredient.

ThingDef.label: chemfuel
ThingDef.description: A volatile liquid chemical. Used to fuel engines and rockets, or to transmute into propellant for projectiles, or as an incendiary weapon.

ThingDef.label: reinforced barrel
ThingDef.description: A large barrel for projectile-based weapons like mortars. In order to hold the high launch pressures, it is specially reinforced and cannot be manufactured at a small scale.

ThingDef.label: potatoes
ThingDef.description: Raw potatoes.

ThingDef.label: raw fungus
ThingDef.description: Raw fungus.

ThingDef.label: rice
ThingDef.description: Raw rice.

ThingDef.label: agave fruit
ThingDef.description: Raw agave fruit.

ThingDef.label: corn
ThingDef.description: Raw corn.

ThingDef.label: berries
ThingDef.description: Assorted berries. Nice to eat, even when raw.

ThingDef.label: hay
ThingDef.description: Nutrient-rich grasses and shoots, harvested and compacted for storage. Hay is good animal feed, but inedible for humans.

ThingDef.label: hops
ThingDef.description: Raw hops. A flavoring and preserving agent that is necessary for making beer.

ThingDef.label: psychoid leaves
ThingDef.description: Raw cut leaves of a psychoid plant. Can be refined into various form of the stimulant drug psychite.

ThingDef.label: smokeleaf leaves
ThingDef.description: Raw cut leaves of a smokeleaf plant. Can be rolled into smokeable joints at a crafting spot.

ThingDef.label: high-explosive shell
ThingDef.description: A shell filled with high explosives. Can be fired from mortars or installed as a trap. Explodes when damaged.

ThingDef.label: incendiary shell
ThingDef.description: A shell filled with flammable gel and a small explosive charge. Starts fires when detonated. Can be fired from mortars or installed as a trap. Explodes when damaged.

ThingDef.label: EMP shell
ThingDef.description: A shell filled with batteries and antennas, for generating an electromagnetic pulse when detonated. Electromagnetic pulses temporarily disable electrical devices and mechanoids. Can be fired from mortars or installed as a trap. Explodes when damaged.

ThingDef.label: smoke shell
ThingDef.description: A shell that generates a cloud of smoke when detonated, obscuring incoming shots and preventing turrets from locking on. Can be fired from mortars or installed as a trap. Explodes when damaged.

ThingDef.label: firefoam shell
ThingDef.description: A pressurized shell filled with fire-retardant foam. Can be fired from mortars or installed as a trap. Explodes when damaged.

ThingDef.label: antigrain warhead
ThingDef.description: An ultra-tech warhead powered by a grain of antimatter. Usually used by spacecraft or glitterworld war machines, it creates a huge explosion and starts fires around the target. Can be fired from mortars or installed as a trap. Explodes when damaged.

ThingDef.label: silver
ThingDef.description: This metal is mostly used as a commodity currency. It can also be used for making decorations.

ThingDef.label: gold
ThingDef.description: The most seductive metal of them all. While it is too soft to be of much practical use, it is strikingly beautiful and never tarnishes. Millions have died in attempting to feed the endless human thirst for gold.

ThingDef.label: steel
ThingDef.description: An iron-carbon metal alloy used for building a huge variety of structures, weapons, and machines.

ThingDef.label: plasteel
ThingDef.description: Advanced spacer tech structural material. Plasteel is extremely strong due to its unique molecular structure.

ThingDef.label: wood
ThingDef.description: Wood from trees or other fibrous plants. Useful for building structures and weapons. It is a good fuel for campfires and generators, and can be refined into chemfuel. In a pinch, a piece of wood can be used as a weapon or a leg.

ThingDef.label: uranium
ThingDef.description: A dark, heavy metal. While it is best known as a fuel for nuclear devices, its extreme density and hardness also make it good for making certain weapons, armor, and ammunition.

ThingDef.label: jade
ThingDef.description: A hard, green stone. Because of its beauty and rarity, jade is often used for ornaments and decorations. Its hardness and density also makes it a good material for blunt weapons.

ThingDef.label: cloth
ThingDef.description: Cloth woven from organic fibers.

ThingDef.label: synthread
ThingDef.description: Spacer-tech synthetic fabric designed for making ordinary clothes. It is soft, light, strong, and insulates well.

ThingDef.label: devilstrand
ThingDef.description: Fabric spun from microfibers extracted from devilstrand mushrooms. It is very tough, good at insulating, and protects exceptionally well against flame.

ThingDef.label: hyperweave
ThingDef.description: Nano-fibers woven into sheets molecule-by-molecule using specialized production mechanites. While it flexes freely most of the time, it stiffens to absorb blows as they land, and is incredibly difficult to break. The secrets of its production are known only to the most advanced glitterworld cultures.

ThingDef.label: sheep wool
ThingDef.description: Sheep's wool. It provides good insulation.

ThingDef.label: alpaca wool
ThingDef.description: The remarkably soft wool of an alpaca. It is warm, protects well from heat, and fetches a high price.

ThingDef.label: megasloth wool
ThingDef.description: While somewhat coarse, megasloth wool's long fibers make it very strong. It is exceptionally warm.

ThingDef.label: muffalo wool
ThingDef.description: Soft, light and provides very good insulation. Muffalo wool clothes can keep the body warm even in very cold conditions.

ThingDef.label: bison wool
ThingDef.description: Thick and coarse wool of a bison. Quite warm.

ThingDef.Name: LeatherBase
ThingDef.description: Tanned, dried, scraped skin. A good traditional material for making clothes and bags.

ThingDef.label: wolfskin
ThingDef.description: A soft furry pelt harvested from a wolf-like creature. It is difficult to pierce and insulates well against cold.

ThingDef.label: panthera fur
ThingDef.description: A soft furry pelt harvested from a big cat. It is difficult to pierce and insulates well against heat.

ThingDef.label: camelhide
ThingDef.description: Tanned, dried, scraped camel skin. Good at temperature regulation in hot climates.

ThingDef.label: bluefur
ThingDef.description: The furry pelt of muffalo. Recognizable by its distinctive blue tint. Good at temperature regulation in cold climates.

ThingDef.label: bearskin
ThingDef.description: The strong furry leather of a bear. Compared to most leather, it is quite a bit tougher and a bit better at all kinds of temperature regulation.

ThingDef.label: guinea pig fur
ThingDef.description: Sheets of guinea pig fur. It is delicate, but luxurious.

ThingDef.label: human leather
ThingDef.description: Tanned, dried, scraped human skin. Most people find this material horrifying. Some find it fascinating. While a decent leather, it neither protects nor insulates particularly well.

ThingDef.label: pigskin
ThingDef.description: Tanned, dried, scraped pig skin. While a decent leather, it neither protects nor insulates particularly well.

ThingDef.label: lightleather
ThingDef.description: Lightweight, thin leather. Probably harvested from a small animal. Not as protective as thicker leathers.

ThingDef.label: birdskin
ThingDef.description: Tanned, dried, scraped bird skin. It is quite delicate. Without its feathers, it provides little protection from heat or cold.

ThingDef.label: chinchilla fur
ThingDef.description: Tanned, dried, scraped chinchilla skin. Known as an extremely luxurious and insulating fur, it is exceptionally valuable.

ThingDef.label: foxfur
ThingDef.description: The pelt of a fox. It protects well from the cold and is quite luxurious, fetching a high price.

ThingDef.label: lizardskin
ThingDef.description: The tanned skin of a cold-blooded reptile. Lizardskin is reasonably tough, but does not insulate well at all.

ThingDef.label: elephant leather
ThingDef.description: Tanned, dried, scraped elephant skin. While quite tough, it is a poor insulator.

ThingDef.label: heavy fur
ThingDef.description: Thick leather covered in a long, rugged mat of fur. Harvested from a large, hardy animal. This thick skin insulates and protects very well.

ThingDef.label: rhinoceros leather
ThingDef.description: Tanned, dried, scraped rhinocerous skin. It is exceptionally durable in combat, but provides little protection from weather.

ThingDef.label: thrumbofur
ThingDef.description: Furry pelt of a thrumbo. Luxurious and extraordinarily durable. Used for the highest-quality crafts for its insulation and strength.

ThingDef.label: patchleather
ThingDef.description: A weak textile created by cutting up and sewing together various types of leathers. Regardless of what kind of leather is used to create it, patchleather's irregular seams make it less tough and less insulating than any intact leather.

ThingDef.label: unfinished sculpture
ThingDef.description: An unfinished sculpture.

ThingDef.label: unfinished gun
ThingDef.description: An unfinished gun of some kind.

ThingDef.label: unfinished weapon
ThingDef.description: An unfinished weapon.

ThingDef.label: unfinished simple armor
ThingDef.description: An unfinished piece of simple armor.

ThingDef.Name: UnfinishedTechArmor
ThingDef.label: unfinished advanced armor
ThingDef.description: An unfinished piece of high-tech armor.

ThingDef.label: unfinished metal armor
ThingDef.description: An unfinished piece of metal armor.

ThingDef.label: unfinished apparel
ThingDef.description: An unfinished piece of an apparel.

ThingDef.label: unfinished belt
ThingDef.description: An unfinished piece of a belt.

ThingDef.label: unfinished pack
ThingDef.description: An unfinished piece of a pack.

ThingDef.label: unfinished component
ThingDef.description: An unfinished component.

ThingDef.label: unfinished prosthetic
ThingDef.description: An unfinished prosthetic.

ThingDef.label: unfinished bionic
ThingDef.description: An unfinished bionic.

ThingDef.label: unfinished mask
ThingDef.description: An unfinished mask.

ThingDef.label: shield belt
ThingDef.description: A projectile-repulsion device. It will attempt to stop incoming projectiles or shrapnel, but does nothing against melee attacks or heat. It prevents the wearer from firing out, and shuts down instantly if hit by EMP.

ThingDef.Name: CowboyHat
ThingDef.label: cowboy hat
ThingDef.description: Stylish yet rugged, this hat keeps the sun and rain off - and it gives anyone who wears it a bit of extra charm. It is the most important part of traditional western attire.

ThingDef.label: bowler hat
ThingDef.description: A good-looking hat which projects a slightly urban, money-loving style. Improves social impact.

ThingDef.label: tribal headdress
ThingDef.description: Elegant traditional garb, often with religious significance. Improves social impact.

ThingDef.label: tuque
ThingDef.description: A soft, thick cap. Great for keeping warm in winter.

ThingDef.label: war mask
ThingDef.description: An artistically terrifying war mask. It hides the wearer's face and makes them more confident.

ThingDef.label: veil
ThingDef.description: A piece of fabric which covers the wearer's face. It protects surprisingly well against pollution.

ThingDef.label: simple helmet
ThingDef.description: A simple helmet which gives moderate protection against sharp attacks. Not effective against blunt weapons.

ThingDef.label: flak helmet
ThingDef.description: A lightweight combat helmet with a complex design, reinforced with plasteel. Not effective against blunt weapons.

ThingDef.label: marine helmet
ThingDef.description: A marine armor helmet, with a built-in status computer and layered plasteel-weave plates.\n\nArmor like this is often used by rapid-incursion space marines.

ThingDef.label: recon helmet
ThingDef.description: A high-tech armored helmet with a built-in status computer and a protective plasteel-weave plate.\n\nArmor like this is often used by imperial scout troops or glitterworld police forces.

ThingDef.label: psychic foil helmet
ThingDef.description: A thin helmet containing finely-tuned sheets of psychically-absorptive foil. Reduces the impact of psychic waves.

ThingDef.label: hood
ThingDef.description: A draped hood which covers the head and ears.

ThingDef.label: smokepop pack
ThingDef.description: A defensive smokescreen. When activated, it will release a cloud of smoke, obscuring incoming shots and preventing turrets from locking on.

ThingDef.label: firefoam pop pack
ThingDef.description: A utility pack made for firefighters. When triggered, a burst of fire-retardant foam is released, covering a wide circle around its wearer.

ThingDef.label: psychic shock lance
ThingDef.description: A limited-use psychic effector. It shocks the target's mind with chaotic images, blocking coherent perception and dropping them into a state of psychic shock. There is a risk of brain damage. It has a long range, but requires line of sight.

ThingDef.label: psychic insanity lance
ThingDef.description: A limited-use psychic effector. It overwhelms the target's mind with terrifying perceptual distortions, driving them into a berserk state. There is a risk of brain damage. It has a long range, but requires line of sight.

ThingDef.label: tribalwear
ThingDef.description: A full-body garment crafted using neolithic tools. While it may look primitive, it is effective at insulating the wearer.

ThingDef.label: parka
ThingDef.description: A parka for staying warm in even the coldest of temperatures.

ThingDef.label: pants
ThingDef.description: A simple set of pants.

ThingDef.label: T-shirt
ThingDef.description: A simple T-shirt.
A nice-looking collared shirt with buttons.
ThingDef.label: button-down shirt

ThingDef.description: A long duster coat for blocking the sun and grit of the outdoors.
ThingDef.label: duster
jacket
ThingDef.description: A tough jacket to stop scrapes and bruises, and to keep one warm in chilly weather.

ThingDef.label: plate armor
ThingDef.description: Overlapping solid plates of armor covering the entire body from neck to feet.

ThingDef.label: flak vest
ThingDef.description: A vest with armor plates inserted on the chest and back. While quite effective at deflecting gunshots and stabbing attacks against the chest, it does nothing to protect the limbs.

ThingDef.label: flak pants
ThingDef.description: A pair of pants with armor plates sewn in. While it's not as good as solid armor, it offers effective protection against all manner of attacks while remaining quite comfortable.

ThingDef.label: flak jacket
ThingDef.description: A tough fabric jacket with armor plates sewn in. While it's not as good as solid armor, it offers effective protection against all manner of attacks while remaining quite comfortable.

ThingDef.label: marine armor
ThingDef.description: A suit of powered armor. Layered plasteel-weave plates are very effective at stopping attacks, with few vulnerable joint sections. Neuro-memetic assistors allow a human to wear the armor and still move easily.\n\nArmor like this is often used by rapid-incursion space marines.

ThingDef.label: recon armor
ThingDef.description: A suit of light partially-powered armor, designed to permit quick movement. Lightweight plasteel-weave plates block attacks without compromising mobility, and neuro-memetic assistors in the lower body allow a human to wear the armor and still move easily.\n\nArmor like this is often used by imperial scout troops and glitterworld police forces.

ThingDef.label: cape
ThingDef.description: A long cape of elegant design. It hangs over one side of the torso.

ThingDef.label: robe
ThingDef.description: A long, flowing robe without a hood.

ThingDef.label: chemfuel puddle
ThingDef.description: A puddle of flammable chemfuel.

ThingDef.Name: ChunkRockBase
ThingDef.description: A chunk of rock. Can be cut into usable stone blocks.

ThingDef.Name: StoneBlocksBase
ThingDef.description: Blocks of stone. Mostly useful for building long-lasting, simple structures.

ThingDef.Name: ChunkSlagSteel
ThingDef.label: steel slag chunk
ThingDef.description: A chunk of steel slag. While it's useless in its current form, it can be smelted to recover steel.

ThingDef.Name: SandstoneBase
ThingDef.label: sandstone
ThingDef.description: A sedimentary rock composed of sand particles compressed together.

ThingDef.label: smoothed sandstone
ThingDef.description: A sedimentary rock composed of sand particles compressed together. The sand layers have been polished to a flat, smooth surface.

ThingDef.label: sandstone blocks
ThingDef.description: Blocks of solid sandstone. Sandstone is a relatively soft rock and chips easily.

RecipeDef.label: make sandstone blocks
RecipeDef.description: Cuts sandstone chunks into usable blocks.

ThingDef.Name: GraniteBase
ThingDef.label: granite
ThingDef.description: A very hard igneous rock.

ThingDef.label: smoothed granite
ThingDef.description: A very hard igneous rock. The shining surface is filled with a mosaic of black, white, and pink speckles.

ThingDef.label: granite blocks
ThingDef.description: Blocks of solid granite. Granite is a very hard stone.

RecipeDef.label: make granite blocks
RecipeDef.description: Cuts granite chunks into usable blocks.

ThingDef.Name: LimestoneBase
ThingDef.label: limestone
ThingDef.description: A sedimentary rock formed from the compacted remains of ancient seashells.

ThingDef.label: smoothed limestone
ThingDef.description: A sedimentary rock formed from the compacted remains of ancient seashells. It glows a smooth white, with light patterns of impurities suspended within.

ThingDef.label: limestone blocks
ThingDef.description: Blocks of solid limestone.

RecipeDef.label: make limestone blocks
RecipeDef.description: Cuts limestone chunks into usable blocks.

ThingDef.Name: SlateBase
ThingDef.label: slate
ThingDef.description: A dark-colored metamorphic rock. Its fine layers are emblematic of slaty cleavage.

ThingDef.label: smoothed slate
ThingDef.description: A dark-colored metamorphic rock. Its fine layers are emblematic of slaty cleavage. Interior strata are clearly visible through the polished surface.

ThingDef.label: slate blocks
ThingDef.description: Blocks of solid slate. A dull-looking rock that chips easily.

RecipeDef.label: make slate blocks
RecipeDef.description: Cuts slate chunks into usable blocks.

ThingDef.Name: MarbleBase
ThingDef.label: marble
ThingDef.description: A soft metamorphic rock.

ThingDef.label: smoothed marble
ThingDef.description: A soft metamorphic rock. This semi-transparent rock almost appears to glow with its own inner light.

ThingDef.label: marble blocks
ThingDef.description: Blocks of solid marble. Marble is a soft, beautiful stone, known for being easy to sculpt.

RecipeDef.label: make marble blocks
RecipeDef.description: Cuts marble chunks into usable blocks.

ThingDef.label: breach axe
ThingDef.description: A combined blade and tool-head attached to a sturdy haft. While slightly less effective than other weapons against human enemies, it excels at tearing down walls, doors, and other structures thanks to its integrated tool-head.

ThingDef.label: mace
ThingDef.description: A refined club, engineered for efficient swinging and deadly impacts.

ThingDef.label: gladius
ThingDef.description: A short sword of ancient design. Good for stabbing or slashing. It's light and nimble, which sometimes lets it beat bigger, heavier weapons.

ThingDef.label: longsword
ThingDef.description: The ancient weapon of kings, the longsword can be used for slashing or stabbing.

ThingDef.label: club
ThingDef.description: A shaped stick, heavy at one end, for bashing enemies to death. This weapon is so old it's part of human biology. Evolutionary biologists say that a major reason humans can tilt our wrists side-to-side (instead of just forward-and-back like other primates) is to be able to better swing a club.

ThingDef.label: knife
ThingDef.description: One of mankind's oldest manufactured objects. The knife has taken many forms, but the concept has always remained the same: A handle for holding and a sharp edge for cutting.

ThingDef.label: ikwa
ThingDef.description: A short spearhandle attached to a long bladed point, designed to be driven into vital organs with a quick thrust.

ThingDef.label: spear
ThingDef.description: A polearm tipped with a sharp point for stabbing opponents.

ThingDef.label: revolver
ThingDef.description: An ancient pattern double-action revolver. It's not very powerful, but has a decent range for a pistol and is quick on the draw.

ThingDef.label: autopistol
ThingDef.description: An ancient pattern blowback-operated self-loading pistol. It lacks stopping power and range, but is quick to fire.

ThingDef.label: machine pistol
ThingDef.description: A micro-submachine gun. It is short-ranged, but very light in the hands. Its rate of fire tends to make up for its weakness.

ThingDef.label: incendiary launcher
ThingDef.description: A wide-barreled incendiary bolt launcher. The bolts create small incendiary explosions on impact, starting fires.

ThingDef.label: smoke launcher
ThingDef.description: A wide-barreled smoke shell launcher. The shell will upon impact release a cloud of smoke, obscuring incoming shots and preventing turrets from locking on.

ThingDef.label: EMP launcher
ThingDef.description: A wide-barreled EMP shell launcher. The shell will upon impact release a burst of electromagnetic energy, stunning mechanical targets (mechanoids, turrets, mortars) and depleting shields in the area of effect.

ThingDef.label: bolt-action rifle
ThingDef.description: An ancient pattern bolt-action rifle. With its long range, and low fire rate, it is unlikely to drive animals to revenge, which makes it a favorite weapon for hunting.

ThingDef.label: pump shotgun
ThingDef.description: An ancient design of shotgun that emits a tight-packed spray of pellets. Deadly, but short range.

ThingDef.label: chain shotgun
ThingDef.description: A magazine-fed fully automatic shotgun. It is even shorter-ranged than a typical shotgun, but is extraordinarily dangerous due to burst fire.

ThingDef.label: heavy SMG
ThingDef.description: A compact, wide-caliber slug-thrower. It's got a very short range, but it packs a punch and handles quite well.

ThingDef.label: LMG
ThingDef.description: A gas-operated light machine gun. While it is somewhat unwieldy and inaccurate, its long bursts of fire are effective against groups of enemies.

ThingDef.label: assault rifle
ThingDef.description: A general-purpose gas-operated assault rifle for field or urban combat. It has good range, decent power, and good accuracy.

ThingDef.label: sniper rifle
ThingDef.description: An ancient design of precision sniper rifle. Bolt action. It has an exceptionally long range, great accuracy and good power. Because it's so unwieldy, other weapons outclass it at close range.

ThingDef.label: minigun
ThingDef.description: A multi-barrel machine gun. It's unwieldy, but once it starts firing it fires very fast. Where most self-loading guns are powered by the energy from the gunpowder, the minigun uses an electric motor to rapidly cycle cartridges through the weapon.

ThingDef.label: triple rocket launcher
ThingDef.description: A single-use rocket launcher that fires three large-bore explosive rockets. Good against small groups of tough targets.\n\nBecause of its unwieldiness, single-use limitation, and the massive destruction it causes, it's said that one must be slightly crazy to use this weapon.

ThingDef.label: doomsday rocket launcher
ThingDef.description: A single-use rocket launcher that fires a massive explosive projectile. Good against large groups of soft targets. Starts fires.\n\nBecause of its unwieldiness, single-use limitation, and the massive destruction it causes, it's said that one must be slightly crazy to use this weapon.

ThingDef.label: frag grenades
ThingDef.description: Old-school fragmentation grenades. They can be thrown a short distance, where they'll explode, damaging anything and anyone nearby.

ThingDef.label: molotov cocktails
ThingDef.description: Glass bottles filled with flammable liquid, with a burning cloth in the neck. A favorite weapon of hooligans and desperate warriors from rim to rim.

ThingDef.label: EMP grenades
ThingDef.description: Electromagnetic pulse grenades damaging to electronic equipment.

ThingDef.Name: Gun_ChargeBlasterHeavyBase
ThingDef.label: heavy charge blaster
ThingDef.description: A pulse-charged rapid-fire blaster for area suppressive fire. Heavy cooling allows long, deadly bursts.

ThingDef.Name: Gun_InfernoCannonBase
ThingDef.label: inferno cannon
ThingDef.description: An incendiary-shot mini-artillery device. It fires a large incendiary warhead.

ThingDef.Name: NeedleGunBase
ThingDef.label: needle gun
ThingDef.description: A long-range weapon used by mechanoids. Named after its needle-like projectiles, it fires single shots with great accuracy. While it does less damage than charge weapons, it can reach over very long distances.

ThingDef.label: short bow
ThingDef.description: A simple short selfbow made from a single piece of wood.

ThingDef.label: pila
ThingDef.description: Pila are spears for throwing. They take a long time to throw, but one hit can do heavy damage. This weapon represents a bundle of pila and can be thrown over and over. The singular of pila is pilum.

ThingDef.label: recurve bow
ThingDef.description: A recurve bow. Its construction behaves like a tuned spring, storing energy more efficiently and delivering a faster shot.

ThingDef.label: greatbow
ThingDef.description: A powerful greatbow. Fires a heavy arrow long distances.

ThingDef.label: charge rifle
ThingDef.description: A charged-shot assault rifle. Pulse-charge technology charges each shot with unstable energy as it leaves the barrel. Released on impact, the charged energy greatly increases the damage done.

ThingDef.label: charge lance
ThingDef.description: A pulse-charged rail-assisted lance weapon. It fires a single shot at high velocity, charging it with unstable energy as it leaves the acceleration rail.

ThingDef.label: orbital bombardment targeter
ThingDef.description: An ancient targeting apparatus for an orbital bombardment system. This unit designates a target and transmits the coordinates to a network of satellites, which then bombard the target area with kinetic impactors. This unit has been reprogrammed to accept unauthorized users, but once it is used, the network will detect the incursion and cut off the link permanently.

ThingDef.label: orbital power beam targeter
ThingDef.description: An ancient targeting unit for a network of power-collection satellites. Once aimed at a target, it directs ancient satellites to begin beaming power down in a massive column of electromagnetic energy. This power can safely be collected in a giant absorption dish. Since you have no absorption dish, you'll be aiming it at enemies, at which point the power column will turn the area into a thousand-degree inferno. This will last until the satellites detect the unsafe targeting, shut themselves down, and permanently deactivate the targeter.

ThingDef.label: tornado generator
ThingDef.description: An ancient control unit for a network of weather-control satellites. This device has had certain failsafes bypassed; it is capable of causing a massive air current disturbance, which will generate a tornado at a chosen location. The weather network will detect this unauthorized intrusion and lock out the device after use, but the tornado will be left to spend its energy normally.

ThingDef.label: thump cannon
ThingDef.description: A breaching explosive launcher used by mechanoids. It fires a concussion bomb that is extremely effective against walls and structures, but does much less damage to small targets.

ThingDef.label: glowstool
ThingDef.description: A small brown mushroom typically found in caves. It smells like an old, dirty rag pulled from the stomach of a rotting muffalo - but it tastes surprisingly good when cooked. Dies when exposed to light.

ThingDef.label: agarilux
ThingDef.description: An enormous purple mushroom. Its size and glowing protrusions make this fungus beautiful to look at. It dies when exposed to light.

ThingDef.label: bryolux
ThingDef.description: A blue moss typically found in deep, dark caves. It is sticky, with tangled fibers, which slows anyone walking over it. Dies when exposed to light.

ThingDef.label: rose
ThingDef.description: A beautiful cultivated flower, the rose has been a symbol of love since Earth's ancient era.

ThingDef.label: daylily
ThingDef.description: A cultivated flower with wide petals and a short lifespan. Daylilies are very beautiful, but must be replanted often.

ThingDef.label: rice plant
ThingDef.description: A short, fast-growing crop that yields small edible grains. Its great nutritional output and ease of cultivation has made it the economic core of many great civilizations. While rice grows quickly, it is sensitive to soil fertility and will not fare well in poor soil.

ThingDef.Name: PotatoPlant
ThingDef.label: potato plant
ThingDef.description: A highly nutritious tuber. Potatoes grow well even in somewhat poor soil, and form a delicious crispy outer coating when fried in oil.

ThingDef.label: corn plant
ThingDef.description: A tall grain plant which produces ears of soft, edible seeds. While corn takes a long time to grow, it yields lots of food compared to other crops. Harvested corn takes a long time to spoil.

ThingDef.label: strawberry plant
ThingDef.description: A low bush-like plant that yields fragile but delicious strawberries. While it isn't quite as productive calorie-for-calorie as other crops, strawberries are delicious even when raw.

ThingDef.label: haygrass
ThingDef.description: A mixture of nutrient-rich grasses which yield large amounts of hay. Hay is edible for animals, but not humans.

ThingDef.label: cotton plant
ThingDef.description: A mid-size crop that yields fine white cotton fibers. These are used to make cloth.

ThingDef.label: devilstrand
ThingDef.description: This fragile mushroom was genetically engineered to produce a silk net that is both difficult to tear and soft to the touch. While the mushroom takes a very long time to grow, only exotic ultra-tech fabrics outperform its devilstrand fibers.\n\nSome say it's called devilstrand because of its red color. Others think it owes its name to the greed it inspires in people.

ThingDef.label: healroot
ThingDef.description: A slow-growing plant which yields herbal medicine when harvested. Sowing and harvesting healroot are both very labor-intensive tasks because of its delicate shoots.\n\nHealroot was selectively bred for centuries by settlers. It is sometimes also called "healer's hand" by tribespeople - a nickname it owes to its five major medicinal virtues.

ThingDef.label: hop plant
ThingDef.description: A flowering crop that yields hops, an essential ingredient in beer.

ThingDef.label: smokeleaf plant
ThingDef.description: A leafy crop grown for the psychological effects of chemicals in its leaves. Smokeleaf leaves can be prepared into joints at the crafting spot. Smokeleaf makes a user feel relaxed, but reduces motivation, and can be addictive.

ThingDef.label: psychoid plant
ThingDef.description: A leafy plant which generates the chemical compound psychite. Originally evolved as a defense mechanism to ward off plant-eating animals by overstimulating and sickening them, the psychite drug can be extracted and refined into various forms for recreational use. It is addictive.

ThingDef.label: cocoa tree
ThingDef.description: A tropical tree that produces chocolate, genetically engineered to sweeten its own product, and survive in slightly less-warm climates.

ThingDef.label: burned stump
ThingDef.description: A burned tree stump. It's ugly and yields very little usable wood.

ThingDef.Name: StumpChoppedBase
ThingDef.label: chopped stump
ThingDef.description: A stump left behind after a tree has been felled. The stump can be extracted but yields very little usable wood. Left outdoors, the stump will deteriorate in time.

ThingDef.Name: StumpSmashedBase
ThingDef.label: smashed stump
ThingDef.description: The remnants of a tree destroyed by damage. It's ugly. The stump can be extracted but yields very little usable wood. Left outdoors, the stump will deteriorate in time.

ThingDef.label: ambrosia bush
ThingDef.description: A rare wild bush which yields the ambrosia fruit. Ambrosia fruit is delicious and produces a drug-like mood boost. Ambrosia cannot be farmed, which makes wild ambrosia groves very valuable.\n\nIts rarity, beauty, and desirability are why ambrosia was named after the food of the ancient Greek gods.

ThingDef.label: tinctoria
ThingDef.description: A genetically-engineered flower-like crop which secretes a self-altering dye. Tinctoria dye can be coaxed into different colors and used to change the color of walls, buildings, and more.

ThingDef.label: dye
ThingDef.description: Dye extracted from a tinctoria plant. It can be used to change the color of walls, buildings, and more.

ThingDef.label: agave
ThingDef.description: A large-leafed desert plant with edible flowers and stalks.

ThingDef.label: pincushion cactus
ThingDef.description: A short cactus. It is so named because it resembles a pincushion.

ThingDef.label: saguaro cactus
ThingDef.description: A large cactus native to arid Earth environments. Though it is not a tree, it yields a small amount of fibrous material that can be used like wood.

ThingDef.label: drago tree
ThingDef.description: A hardy desert tree topped with thick, pointed leaves.

ThingDef.label: grass
ThingDef.description: Wild grass. Grows anywhere there is a little light and minimally fertile ground.

ThingDef.label: tall grass
ThingDef.description: Wild tall grass. Slows down anyone moving over it.

ThingDef.label: bush
ThingDef.description: A short shrub. Does not typically talk.

ThingDef.label: brambles
ThingDef.description: Tangled, thorny, woody shoots covered with leaves. Brambles grow in clusters, and slow down anyone moving over them.

ThingDef.label: wild healroot
ThingDef.description: A slow-growing plant which yields herbal medicine when harvested.\n\nThis wild breed of healroot is hardier than domesticated healroot, but too difficult to cultivate. It is prized by tribespeople in colder climates.

ThingDef.label: willow tree
ThingDef.description: One of the fastest growing shade trees, willows provide a beautiful, leafy canopy. It doesn't yield much usable wood.

ThingDef.label: cypress tree
ThingDef.description: A tall coniferous tree often found in swamps. Despite its slow growth, planting these trees can be profitable as a low-effort, long-term investment because they yield so much usable wood.

ThingDef.label: maple tree
ThingDef.description: A common medium-sized tree, easily identifiable by its distinct three-pointed leaf.

ThingDef.label: chokevine
ThingDef.description: Tangled masses of cord-like, spiky vines which coil in great masses along the ground. Chokevine greatly slows down anyone who moves over it. Multiple tribes have independently generated stories of chokevine strangling children to death in the night, as a way to scare kids into coming home before dark.

ThingDef.label: dandelions
ThingDef.description: A tiny yellow flower which grows in large clusters. Though it is often considered a weed, dandelions in bloom are quite beautiful.

ThingDef.label: astragalus
ThingDef.description: A small perennial wildflower that grows in alpine climates.

ThingDef.label: moss
ThingDef.description: Wild moss that grows in clumps in areas of low light and cool temperatures. Moss takes a long time to grow, but is very frost-resistant.

ThingDef.label: berry bush
ThingDef.description: A bushy wild plant which yields delicious berries. Berries can be cooked, but they're also good to eat even when raw.

ThingDef.label: oak tree
ThingDef.description: A hardwood tree. Oaks take a long time to grow, but their wood is so strong that 'oak' is used as a metaphor for strength across many cultures.

ThingDef.label: poplar tree
ThingDef.description: A softwood tree that grows very fast. Unfortunately, its wood is weak and so it yields less useful material than hardwood trees.

ThingDef.label: pine tree
ThingDef.description: A large conifer covered with prickly pine cones. It grows in a distinctive conical shape.

ThingDef.label: birch tree
ThingDef.description: A temperate-biome tree known for its thin, white, paper-like bark.

ThingDef.label: low shrubs
ThingDef.description: Various low broadleaf shrubs. These grow in clusters and slow down movement.

ThingDef.label: alocasia
ThingDef.description: A tropical plant. Its extremely broad leaves are a commonly-recognized signifier of tropical forests.

ThingDef.label: clivia
ThingDef.description: An unusual plant with tall, pretty flowers. Some call it the 'bush lily'.

ThingDef.label: giant rafflesia
ThingDef.description: A rare, giant flower which can be found deep in steaming jungles. You would think a giant flower would be beautiful, but this one looks and smells like rotting flesh.

ThingDef.label: teak tree
ThingDef.description: An exceptionally strong hardwood tree that grows in warm climates. Because teak wood is so durable and water-resistant, it was used to form the keel of wooden sailing ships in ancient times.

ThingDef.label: cecropia tree
ThingDef.description: One of the most common rainforest trees. Cecropia grows very fast, but yields little usable wood.

ThingDef.label: palm tree
ThingDef.description: A tropical tree with a tall, naked trunk topped by a cluster of very broad leaves. Unfortunately, this variety doesn't produce any edible coconuts.

ThingDef.label: bamboo tree
ThingDef.description: A fast-growing tree-like plant that grows in dense groves. Bamboo can be harvested for a wood-like material. The plant itself is not beautiful.

ThingDef.label: grizzly bear
ThingDef.description: A huge omnivorous mammal adapted for cold climates. Bears' thick blubber and fur keeps them warm in winter.\n\nWhile their usual diet consists of fish, berries, honey, and scavenged meat, the grizzly is capable of using its massive strength and deadly claws to kill live prey. They are startlingly quick for such lumbering creatures.

ThingDef.label: polar bear
ThingDef.description: A great white bear adapted for frozen climates. Their thick blubber and fur keep them warm in winter.\n\nWhile their usual diet consists of fish and scavenged meat, the polar bear can also use its massive strength and deadly claws to kill live prey. They are startlingly quick for such lumbering creatures.

ThingDef.label: ostrich
ThingDef.description: The largest unmodified bird species, ostriches are known for their fast run, huge eggs, and powerful kick. It is easily angered.

ThingDef.label: emu
ThingDef.description: A large flightless bird with beady eyes on its ugly face. With its bad attitude, it is the jerk of the natural world. Bother it, and it is guaranteed to seek revenge.

ThingDef.label: cassowary
ThingDef.description: A large flightless bird with brightly-colored feathers. While it looks beautiful, its kick is vicious. It's known for being quick to aggression when harmed by violence or confronted by incompetent animal tamers.

ThingDef.label: cougar
ThingDef.description: One of the most dangerous big cats, cougars are solitary hunters with long, sharp teeth and claws. They stalk prey from hidden positions before pouncing.\n\nWhile humans are not their normal diet, they won't turn down a meal of vulnerable human meat.

ThingDef.label: panther
ThingDef.description: An agile and powerful big cat native to the jungles of old Earth. As solitary ambush predators, panthers are masters of taking down both large and small prey. Onlookers tend to focus on their graceful movements, while those in closer contact usually notice their skull-crushing strength.

ThingDef.label: lynx
ThingDef.description: A wildcat larger than a housecat, but smaller than a cougar. Lynxes survive on a diet of small birds and animals. Their very warm fur keeps them safe from the brutally cold temperatures of their frozen territories.

ThingDef.label: cat
ThingDef.description: One of mankind's first pets, the cat is a small mammal which hunts vermin. Known for their aloofness, cats are nevertheless popular companions because of their independence, calm disposition, and fine, pettable fur.

ThingDef.label: yorkshire terrier
ThingDef.description: A small, even-tempered dog. Originally bred to hunt rats, it later became a show and companionship animal. Some consider it useless, but the mood boost it gives by nuzzling can outweigh the cost of feeding it.

ThingDef.label: guinea pig
ThingDef.description: Neither a pig or a creature from Guinea, these little rodents are bred to be a household pet and a delicious dinner.

ThingDef.label: labrador retriever
ThingDef.description: A very versatile, medium-sized dog. Originally bred to retrieve birds shot on the hunt, the lab is also an excellent guard dog, play pal, and family friend.

ThingDef.label: husky
ThingDef.description: A large, energetic dog with a thick fur coat for remaining comfortable in arctic environments.

ThingDef.label: monkey
ThingDef.description: A small primate, the monkey can use its curly tail to grab on to branches, leaving its hands free to do other things. Monkeys are selfish but clever, and can be trained to carry out fairly complex tasks.

ThingDef.label: chicken
ThingDef.description: The most traditional farm bird, the chicken is raised for its eggs and meat. It grows very quickly and lays eggs very often.

ThingDef.label: duck
ThingDef.description: A very common type of farm bird, also appearing in the wild, the duck is raised for its delicious meat. It grows quick but lays eggs quite rarely.

ThingDef.label: turkey
ThingDef.description: A short, fat, flightless bird known for its hilarious 'gobbling' call. It has been long domesticated, but also lives in the wild.

ThingDef.label: goose
ThingDef.description: A domesticated bird kept by humans as poultry for it's eggs and meat. Lays eggs very often, however they take a long time to hatch.

ThingDef.label: cow
ThingDef.description: A large domesticated ungulate, cows have been bred for millennia to produce huge amounts of milk, meat, and leather. They are exceptionally gentle creatures and will never seek revenge, no matter how many times they are harmed. Most of them are so adapted to farm life that they cannot survive in the wild.

ThingDef.Name: BoomalopeThingBase
ThingDef.label: boomalope
ThingDef.description: Engineered for chemicals production, the boomalope grows a large sac of volatile chemicals on its back. Though it is weak and fragile for its size, other animals have learned to avoid it because of the huge explosion it produces when it dies. It can be milked to produce chemfuel - very carefully.

ThingDef.label: muffalo
ThingDef.description: A large herding herbivore descended from buffalo and adapted for both cold and warm environments. While enraged muffalo are deadly, tamed muffalo are quite docile and can be used as pack animals.\n\nNobody is quite sure why they're blue - it might even be some early genetic modification test that just never got changed.

ThingDef.label: bison
ThingDef.description: A large plant eating mammal appearing in the savannah wilderness. Tamed are quite docile, but enraged are fast and dangerous.

ThingDef.label: dromedary
ThingDef.description:
A large land mammal adapted to arid environments. Domesticated since ancient times, its leather is exceptionally good at insulating against the desert heat, and its milk is quite nourishing. It can be used as a pack animal and mount, but its bouncing gait makes it slower to ride than a horse.

By storing water in its large humps and reclaiming moisture from its breath as it exhales, it can go weeks without drinking.

When in a caravan, people can ride dromedaries to increase the caravan's speed.

ThingDef.label: goat
ThingDef.description: Naturally curious about the world, goats are among the friendliest domesticated creature bred by mankind.

ThingDef.label: elk
ThingDef.description: A large member of the deer family, well-adapted to life in cold climates. Domesticated elk can be milked, but refuse to carry packs.

ThingDef.label: yak
ThingDef.description: Yaks are robust cattle with a bulky frame, short but thick legs, and rounded cloven hooves that are splayed to help them walk in snow.

ThingDef.label: caribou
ThingDef.description: A large member of the deer family, well-adapted to life in cold climates. Caribou can be milked, but refuse to carry packs.

ThingDef.label: horse
ThingDef.description: A large hoofed mammal with a short coat, a long mane, and a long tail. Horses have been domesticated since ancient times.\n\nWhen in a caravan, people can ride horses to increase the caravan's speed.

ThingDef.label: donkey
ThingDef.description: A small relative of the horse, domesticated in ancient times for farm work. Its goofy call is simultaneously annoying and endearing.\n\nWhen in a caravan, people can ride donkeys to increase the caravan's speed.

ThingDef.label: elephant
ThingDef.description: The largest unmodified land animal. Elephants has a long trunk they use to manipulate objects, and sharp tusks they use to gore attackers. A dead elephant's valuable tusks can be recovered by butchering it.\n\nIntelligent creatures with complex social relationships, elephants can be used as pack animals or trained to carry out the most complex of tasks. They live a long time, and are known to remember events and relationships from many decades before.

ThingDef.label: rhinoceros
ThingDef.description: Despite being herbivorous, this large mammal is very easy to enrage. Once angered, its massive strength and sharp horn make it a brutal opponent. It has more muscle in one leg than most humans do in their whole body.

ThingDef.label: hare
ThingDef.description: This small, solitary herbivore can swiftly hop away from danger.

ThingDef.label: snowhare
ThingDef.description: This hardy animal survives the brutal winters of its homelands by burrowing through snow to find edible plants.

ThingDef.label: megascarab
ThingDef.description: A genetically-engineered war insect that resembles a massive beetle. Once the worker caste of an artificial ecosystem of insects designed to fight mechanoid invasions, it is less deadly than its larger cousins. Still, its size and hard shell make it dangerous when it attacks. A eusocial creature, it cannot reproduce individually.\n\nEngineered to thrive in mechanoid-ravaged environments, war insects like this move faster after being exposed to polluted terrain.

ThingDef.label: spelopede
ThingDef.description: A medium-sized bioengineered insectoid the size of a sheep. The spelopede is the middle caste of a hive, taking care of most work tasks as well as fighting with its digging claws. It's dangerous in combat, but slow on open ground.\n\nEngineered to thrive in mechanoid-ravaged environments, war insects like this move faster after being exposed to polluted terrain.

ThingDef.label: megaspider
ThingDef.description: Not actually a spider, the megaspider is a genetically-engineered giant insect the size of a bear. Its thick chitinous armor makes it hard to kill, while its long ripper-blades make it deadly at close quarters. It is, however, quite slow in open terrain.\n\nEngineered to fight mechanoids in toxic environments, war insects like this move faster after being exposed to polluted terrain.

ThingDef.label: thrumbo
ThingDef.description: A gigantic, graceful creature of unknown origin. The thrumbo is gentle by nature, but extremely dangerous when enraged. While its long fur is exceptionally beautiful, its hide is also incredibly resistant to damage. Its razor-sharp horn fetches a huge price.\n\nLegends say that an old thrumbo is the wisest creature in the universe - it simply chooses not to speak.

ThingDef.label: cobra
ThingDef.description: A large predatory snake. Cobras can be highly aggressive if provoked, and their bite injects toxic venom into the victim.

ThingDef.label: tortoise
ThingDef.description: This heavily armored land-dwelling reptile is known for its slow moving speed and surprisingly vicious bite. Because of its natural armor, it is tough to kill and can do serious damage during drawn-out melee fights.

ThingDef.label: alphabeaver
ThingDef.description: A large beaver-like creature genetically engineered to harvest wood with machine-like efficiency. In the absence of specialized feed, these animals will enter a manic state that compels them to eat trees whole, and are likely to attack if disturbed.

ThingDef.label: pig
ThingDef.description: Pigs were one of the first animals domesticated by humans. They are an efficient source of meat, and are easy to feed because they will eat almost anything.

ThingDef.label: wild boar
ThingDef.description: This hairy omnivore is descended from escaped pigs and evolved for living in the wild.\n\nIts tusks make it a better fighter than its domesticated pig cousins. Unfortunately, it is too unruly to be trained in the most complex tasks.

ThingDef.label: ibex
ThingDef.description: The wild ancestor of the domesticated goat. Ibexes live on marginal territory where most antelopes couldn't survive, eating lichens and sparse mountain plants. They're famous for dextrously hopping across bare cliff faces - and for their violent ramming attack.

ThingDef.label: deer
ThingDef.description: A medium-sized herding herbivore which prefers to live in mixed forests and plains. Deer are very quick.

ThingDef.label: gazelle
ThingDef.description: A small, extremely quick antelope known for its amazingly long leap.

ThingDef.label: chinchilla
ThingDef.description: A small, nimble rodent. Its fur is softer than just about anything in the universe, making it very valuable as a trade good.

ThingDef.label: sheep
ThingDef.description: Sheep husbandry is practiced throughout the majority of the inhabited worlds, however only recently it has been introduced to the rimworlds. Domestic sheep are relatively small herbivores, usually with yellowish wool and medium sized horns.

ThingDef.label: alpaca
ThingDef.description: A medium-sized ungulate closely related to the llama, the alpaca is usually raised for its remarkably soft and insulating wool. Alpacas have also been used as pack animals since they hauled cargo on the rugged mountain trails of ancient South America.

ThingDef.label: megasloth
ThingDef.description: A giant, solitary herbivore with two giant claws for warding off threats. Long extinct after being wiped out by the natives of Earth's American continent, the megasloth was later brought back using advanced cloning and artificial gestators. Its thick hide is exceptionally strong and insulating, and makes a great leather for cold-weather clothing. It is peaceful if left alone, but will shred anyone who disturbs it with its giant claws.

ThingDef.label: capybara
ThingDef.description: The largest natural rodent, the capybara is well-adapted for steaming jungle environments.

ThingDef.label: squirrel
ThingDef.description: One of the many hardy rodent species that follows humankind everywhere it spreads. Squirrels are distinguished by their bushy tails, which they use as umbrellas in bad weather.

ThingDef.Name: RatThingBase
ThingDef.label: rat
ThingDef.description: A widely-hated rodent known for soiling kitchens and spreading disease, rats have a way of following humans everywhere they go. It eats almost anything and lives almost anywhere.

ThingDef.label: boomrat
ThingDef.description: Either by deliberate genetic weaponization, or as an unusual defense mechanism, these rodent-like creatures create a powerful fire-starting explosion when killed.

ThingDef.label: raccoon
