HugsLib.UpdateFeatureDef.content: Hint 1: You can leave ruins event moving your pawns to a green area on map's edge. Hint 2: You can use right mouse button to pick up any stuff while looting abandoned base. You can also load your caravan animals the same way. |Major changes |1) In this version you can't instantly reform caravan between raids during the abandoned base event. That's what you need the hints above for. On my opinion, during this encounter you should manually explore the ruins, find any valuable stuff, pick it up and leave before another hostile party arrives. From now on you won't be able to leave automatically after defeating initial defenders, picking goods lazily from the list. From now on, pick up all valuables and move to the map's edge. Ok, you can actually revert to the old way in mod settings, but I won't recommend. |2) Now contents of graves and cryptosleep pods are captured and spawned. So if you open a cryptosleep pod and find a fatally infected colonist, you can be sure: it's the same colonist as in blueprint source game. And he still has been waiting for a healing serum since long time ago. The mod saves name, appearance, stats, health condition, traits and apparel, and so on (but not an entire pawn, it's still too much info). Also this feature works with corpses laying around and in general, with any containers and their contents. But please note that this will work only for newly captured blueprints, so you probably won't notice anything at first, until the server gets enough new blueprints. And you should probably clear your cache after a week and force loading some data to increase probability of getting additional content. |Minor changes - Replaced most of collapsed rocks with various walls - Dates of all events (including those in art objects) are now consistent across one ruins piece and are always earlier than current date - During most encounters hostile units won't spawn near map's edge, so you can enter relatively safely - Fires and torches are not spawned in ruins - Separate settings for minimum and maximum ruins piece radius - Added ability to reset mod settings to defaults - Now you're not able to claim active turrets during abandoned base encounter - Weapon shelves and other storages are spawned with the lowest storage priority possible, so your pawn won't run across the map to store your weapons - Doors and locks compatibility checked - Fixed bug with ruins placed on water - Now mod tends to load more recent maps - Rebalanced deterioration (now objects most likely won't lose more than 300-500 hit points, so no more "23 of 350000 hit-points" beta-poly walls) - Fixed crash on exit - Speed up loading (for me the game takes the same 70 seconds to load as before, but probably it will help for those who report 40 minutes loading)
Quick fixes of some annoying ruins event bugs.

|Important: this version has significantly reworked internal mechanics, and I'm not completely sure it will work absolutely the same as the previos version. So if you notice ruins generation become worse for you, or if you encounter compatibility or saving problems, please report to steam discussion thread. |Major changes and new features |1) "Pristine ruins" event now has additional info: current wealth and raiders presence. So you can wait nearby before entering to get smaller initial enemy party. Also initial raiders party is toned down and made much more diverse. Now there are several groups of different factions, most likely fighting with each other, so you will face serious danger only if you decide to stay in ruins. |2) Event threat level is tied to game difficulty. For peaceful difficulty level you won't get raids on ruins events |3) Now you can instantly reform caravan if you wait some time (0.5 to 3 days) after defeating the last raid in current ruins location. So if you don't want to pick up things manually, just setup a temporary outpost and wait a couple of days. |4) Your colonists may get a mood boost when visiting ruins. Boost amount is based on ruins wealth. If ruins wealth is too low you'll get a small mood penalty. |5) Now you have an option to disable ruins on your starting location. |Minor changes and bugfixes - Moved blueprints loading to a separate thread, this fixed short freezes on startup - Fixed issue with 100% gear on corpses - Rebalanced ruins density depending on settlement proximity - Blueprint id is selected preliminaly for ruins events, so you can't savescum to get different ruins on each entry - Unfinished items spawn normally

|Planetary Ruins! Now you can visit all bases of all players who played their games on a planet with the same coverage, map size and seed. Some bases will be spawned as ruins (and you can explore them) and some will be spawned as factions' properties, so you can attack them with the same conseqences as for attacking a regular faction base. To load planetary ruins you need to go to Options -> Mod Settings -> Real Ruins - Planetary Ruins and hit the load button. If you're about to start a new game, you can check how many places on the map you can get for a particular seed, map size and planet coverage by visiting https://woolstrand.art Please note that this feature is still in beta and it's highly recommended to make a backup save game before trying. However, this feature won't influence your gameplay in any way until you manually load planetary ruins. |Caravan reforming changes Ok, finally I managed to make caravan reforming in a way it supposed to be. Now you can reform caravan via standard caravan menu, but after that pawns will load caravan in the same way they load it on your home map. They will bring all items to a caravan packing spot and then leave via map edge. And a lot of things may happen while they're doing it! |Other changes There are also a bit of stability changes, less bugs and error messages when importing some kind of maps, no more minified things issues and some more small changes I even can't recall now.

|Caravan forming selector! So, now you can select one of three ways of reforming caravan after ruins event. "Automatic" is a regular reform like you have on your home map. "Instant" is instant reform like in previous version. "Manual" is also one of two previous types where you need to collect all items manually and leave via map edge.

|Caravan forming issue resolved 1. Fixed issue with automatic items unloading upon arriving on event or POI locations. 2. Now both Automatic and Manual caravan forming options work in the same way. They both allow manual items picking and they both allow homemap-style caravan forming (even when there are enemies, so watch your pawns!). Instant caravan reforming option is still available and it works the same way as before, instantly reforming caravan if there are no enemies nearby.
|Version 1.1 compatibility Looks like the mod works again with 1.1 game version.
|Version 1.3 compatibility Looks like the mod works again with 1.3 game version. Updated French translation. New translation by qux.

|SRTS Expanded compatibility added Now you can fly directly to ruins event or world map POI using your ship. The same "drop at edge" and "drop in center" options are accessible. Have fun! Added simplified chinese translation by Juijote. P.S.: some new features are on the way, see here: https://www.patreon.com/posts/60705988
Updated the mod to work with 1.4 game version.

|Planetary ruins on start This major update allows you to load planetary ruins at the very start, even before selecting your starting location. And yes, you can land into any location, even into ruins, either abandoned or not.

ConceptDef.label: Builders will try to mine valuables
ConceptDef.helpText: Note: Placing a building over valuable ore will allow builders to mine the ore. Ore can be wasted if mined with low skill. If your builders are not skilled at mining, you may want to cancel your building project and let skilled miners do their job first.

ConceptDef.label: SS: Sidearms
ConceptDef.helpText:
Simple Sidearms

In order to equip weapons as sidearms, rightclick them and select the Equip as sidearm option.

By default, colonists will use whichever weapon type they are best skilled with or passionate about. Ranged weapon users will also switch to a melee weapon when engaged in close combat. This behaviour can be altered in the mod settings.

ConceptDef.label: SS: Dropping sidearms
ConceptDef.helpText: Sidearms with a gray background are currently in a colonists inventory and eligible for use. Right click to drop.

ConceptDef.label: SS: Missing sidearms
ConceptDef.helpText: Sidearms with a dark purple background are currently missing from a colonists loadout. They will attempt to replace them at earliest opportunity, assuming any can be found. Right click to forget about the sidearm.

ConceptDef.label: SS: Weapon preference
ConceptDef.helpText:
Colonists can have sidearm use configured on an individual basis. The options are: 
Use ranged weapons
Use weapons colonist is passionate about or skilled with 
Use melee weapons

ConceptDef.label: SS: Advanced controls (ranged)
ConceptDef.helpText:
Left click a carried ranged weapon to set it as the default ranged weapon. If the colonist weapon preference is set to ranged (or skill on a colonist more skilled with ranged weapons), this weapon will be what the colonist equips when not in active combat. It will also be used while hunting. 

Click a default ranged weapon again to force its use regardless of range/DPS. 

Right click to remove forced use/default status.

ConceptDef.label: SS: Advanced controls (melee)
ConceptDef.helpText:
Left click a carried melee weapon to set it as the preferred ranged weapon. The colonist will always use this weapon when weapon preference is set to melee (or skill on a colonist more skilled with melee weapons) and when forced into close combat. 

Click a preferred melee weapon again to force its use at all times. 

Right click to remove forced use/preference.

ConceptDef.label: SS: Advanced controls (drafted)
ConceptDef.helpText: Left click a carried weapon while drafted to force its use until end of combat. \n\nNote that most changes to sidearm loadout require the pawn to not be drafted.

ConceptDef.label: SS: Losing weapons
ConceptDef.helpText: Depending on the settings, Simple Sidearms can cause colonists to drop their weapons in a variety of situations (default is attacks in melee). Don't worry - your colonists will retrieve their weapons after the fight. \n\nThis is a customizable feature - take a look in the mod settings dialog to learn more.

ConceptDef.label: SS: CE patch
ConceptDef.helpText: Combat Extended is loaded. SimpleSidearms inventory management functionality is disabled.

HugsLib.UpdateFeatureDef.content: Please remember that Simple Sidearms is designed with customization in mind. Chances are that if a specific feature bothers you, there is an option in the mod settings to disable or alter it.|Pawns now remember their weapons!|img:tuts/havePunch|img:tuts/rememberDropped|Pawns will now remember which weapon is their primary and will switch back to in once undrafted. They will also remember which weapons they are missing when forced to drop them. This includes dropping their primary weapon due to being downed. Once undrafted or done recovering in the hospital, they will automatically go retrieve them.

ResearchProjectDef.label: Terrain Rehabilitation
ResearchProjectDef.description: Allows you to correctly layer dirt on rough stone and other terrains to make underground greenhouses.

TerrainDef.label: soil
TerrainDef.description: Standard soil. Tastes like dirt.

TerrainDef.Name: TS_Tilled
TerrainDef.label: tilled soil
TerrainDef.description: Tilled soil, for planting crops properly.

TweaksGalore.TweakSubSectionDef.label: Habringer Tree
TweaksGalore.TweakSubSectionDef.description: Tweaks specific to the Harbinger tree.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Enable Habringer Tweaks
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: This entire section is disabled by default for compatibility sake, and must be enabled for the tweaks inside it to do anything.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Replantable Harbinger
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Makes it so you can move Harbinger trees like any other.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Show Genes Tab
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: By default the Genes tab is hidden on pawns, if you don't have another mod revealing it, you can use this to do so instead. Just keep in mind this was potentially hidden in vanilla for a reason.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Spawn Pregnancy Chance
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: PawnKinds usually have a 3% chance to spawn pregnant if children are enabled which is multiplied by fertility of the pawn, this lets you change that base chance. Any pawnKind that doesn't use the default value will be skipped so as not to cause problems.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Flatten Complexity
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Remove complexity values from genes so they are all set to 0.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Flatten Metabolism
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Remove metabolism values from genes so they are all set to 0.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Flatten Archites
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Remove archite values from genes so they are all set to 0.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Enabled
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: This controls if any of the mechanitor tweaks even try to function, some tweaks have no other way of knowing if they should even run.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Disable Range Limit
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Makes mechanoids controllable regardless of distance to Mechanitor. If they can design a neural interface they can design something with better than cheap wifi range.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Bandwidth Base
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Controls the initial bandwidth all Mechanitors have.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Control Group Base
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Controls the initial number of control groups all Mechanitors have.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Bandwitdth Per Band Node
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Controls the bandwidth a band node adds to a given mechanitor.

TweaksGalore.TweakSubSectionDef.label: Player Mechanoid Stats
TweaksGalore.TweakSubSectionDef.description: Allows the changing of work stats for player mechanoids so they don't suck nearly as much.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Enabled
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Allows the changing of mechanoid stats, useful for disabling if there's any compatibility issues.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Energy Drain Rate
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Controls the rate at which mechanoid energy drains.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Skill Level
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Controls the skill level all mechanoids have (vanilla is universal like this, it's weird).

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Enable Polux Tweaks
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: This entire section is disabled by default for compatibility sake mostly, some Polux related tweaks function regardless of if they've been changed (any changing a radius for example) so this allows them all to be skipped over without any potential for conflicts if you prefer another polux tweak mod.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Replantable Polux
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Makes it so you can move Polux trees like any other.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Ignore Artificial Buildings
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Vanilla usually disables the tree's effects if there are artificial buildings in its radius, this disables that behaviour and lets it function anyway.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Effect Radius
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: The radius in which the polux tree will cleanse of pollution.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Effect Rate
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: A multiplier on the time between each attempt to cleanse pollution around the tree.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Slave Straps For Nudists
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Makes slave straps acceptable for nudists, it makes no real sense that they'd be clothes so this feels like a bugfix honestly.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: You Look Fine!
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Stops pawns from changing their look at the style bench every five goddamn minutes, it's a story simulator not Barbies Makeup Challenge.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Darklight Glow Pods
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Makes glow pods spawned in insectoid nests use the darklight colour.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Disable Desired Apparel
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Disables default Ideology desired apparel from showing up, that random shit that factions use throughout them for no fucking reason.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: No Meme Limit
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Raises the limit of how many memes you can choose to 1000...so effectively no limit.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Proper Suppression
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Changes suppression mechanics slightly so that rebellions never happen if your slaves are kept suppressed. Also prevents suppressed pawns from taking part in rebellions when they do happen.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Suppression Threshold
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Controls the percentage at which rebellions are considered suppressed, if Proper Suppression is enabled this is the threshold at which rebellions would be disabled entirely.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Unlocked Ideology Buildings
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Removes the meme restriction on ideology buildings so you can use them regardless of what memes you have. Includes floors and apparel.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Enable Gauranlen Tweaks
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: This entire section is disabled by default for compatibility sake mostly, some Gauranlen related tweaks function regardless of if they've been changed (any changing a radius for example) so this allows them all to be skipped over without any potential for conflicts if you prefer another gauranlen tweak mod.

TweaksGalore.TweakSubSectionDef.label: Gauranlen Tree
TweaksGalore.TweakSubSectionDef.description: Tweaks specific to the Gauranlen tree itself.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Replantable Gauranlen
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Makes it so you can move Gauranlen trees like any other.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Artificial Building Radius
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: The radius in which a debuff is applied to the trees effects if artificial buildings are built in it.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Initial Connection Range
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Initial connection strength will be a random value in this range.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Connection Gain
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: The amount of connection gained for each hour of pruning.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Connection Loss
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: A multiplier on the loss rate of the connection.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Connection Loss From Buildings
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: A multiplier on the loss rate of the connection specifically due to artificial buildings in range.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Moss Growth Radius
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: The radius in which gauranlen moss will grow inside.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Moss Growth Days
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: The number of days it takes for gauranlen moss to grow to maturity.

TweaksGalore.TweakSubSectionDef.label: Dryads
TweaksGalore.TweakSubSectionDef.description: Tweaks specific to the dryads that come from the Gauranlen Tree.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Max Dryads
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Max number of dryads when connection is full. This is technically done on a point curve with multiple values, but to keep it simple I just distribute the max linearly through it.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Dryad Spawn Days
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Number of days between the spawning of Dryads.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Dryad Cocoon Days
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Number of days Dryads remain in their cocoons.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Gaumaker Cocoon Days
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Number of days Gaumaker Dryads remain in their cocoons.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Gaumaker Pod Days
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Number of days it takes for a Gaumaker pod to mature.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Gaumaker Seed Yield
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Number of seeds obtained from a Gaumaker pod.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: No Biocoding
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: If enabled, removes biocoding from weapons so they don't spawn with it. Does not affect any that have already spawned but will affect mod added ones.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: No Death Acidifiers
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: If enabled, removes death acidifiers from pawnKinds so they don't spawn with them. Does not affect any pawns that have already spawned, but will affect mod added pawns.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Pinata Death Acidifiers
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: If enabled, changes death acidifier functionality to instead drop all equipment on the ground, and instantly dessicate the pawn. As opposed to their vanilla behaviour of destroying the equipment. Cus why not? Everyone loves a loot pinata.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Allow Any Buildings In Throneroom
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: If enabled, removes building restrictions in thronerooms. Includes Altars.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Allow Altar in Throneroom
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: If enabled, specifically allows altars to be built in thronerooms. Pointless if 'any' are allowed already.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Delayed Royalty
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Delays the Royalty starter quests by a few days more than usual to give additional time to get ready for them.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Free Meditation
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Allows any pawn to use any meditation focus building regardless of the focus types they have. Automatically patches all vanilla and modded meditation sources.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: No Backstory Limits
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Allows any pawn to use Natural or Artistic meditation focus types regardless of backstory. If Vanilla Psycasts Expanded is active, this will also handle the psycaster paths being unlockable.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: No Trading Permit
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: If enabled, removes the need to have a permit to trade with the Shattered Empire.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Uninstallable Mech Shields
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: If enabled, allows you to uninstall mech cluster shields for your own use. This also prevents them shutting down when the cluster is cleared so they remain useful.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Wait, This Is Better
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Adds previous tier tags to all royal acceptable apparel (including modded) so that apprel of a higher tier will satisfy pawns looking for a lower tier. Should really be the default.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Enable Anima Tweaks
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: This entire section is disabled by default for compatibility sake mostly, some Anima related tweaks function regardless of if they've been changed (any changing a radius for example) so this allows them all to be skipped over without any potential for conflicts if you prefer another anima tweak mod.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Anima Grass Per Psylink Level
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: The values are the amount of grass needed to be grown on top of what was already needed for the previous level.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Meditation Psyfocus Gain Rate
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: The amount of psyfocus a pawn gains per day of mediation.

TweaksGalore.TweakSubSectionDef.label: Anima Scream
TweaksGalore.TweakSubSectionDef.description: Tweaks specific to the anima scream from when you cut down the anima tree.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Disable Anima Scream
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Disables the Anima Scream debuff from chopping them down.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Anima Scream Debuff
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: The impact on mood from the thought applied.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Anima Scream Duration
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: The duration on the thought applied, in days.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Anima Scream Stack Limit
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: The stack limit for the thought applied.

TweaksGalore.TweakSubSectionDef.label: Anima Tree
TweaksGalore.TweakSubSectionDef.description: Tweaks specific to the anima tree itself.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Replantable Anima
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Makes it so you can move Anima trees like any other.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Artificial Building Radius
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: The radius in which a debuff is applied to the trees effects if artificial buildings are built in it.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Natural Building Radius
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: The radius in which a buff is applied to the trees effects for natural buildings.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Natural Building Max
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: The maximum number of buildings which can buff the Anima Tree.

TweaksGalore.TweakSubSectionDef.label: Anima Shrines
TweaksGalore.TweakSubSectionDef.description: These are specific to the nature shrines that can be built to enhance the Anima tree.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Nature Shrines Always Buildable
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Nature Shrines are usually only buildable when you have a nature based Psycaster, this unlocks that limitation.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Artificial Building Radius
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: The radius in which a debuff is applied to the trees effects if artificial buildings are built in it.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Natural Building Radius
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: The radius in which a buff is applied to the trees effects for natural buildings.

TweaksGalore.TweakSubSectionDef.label: Better Gloomlight
TweaksGalore.TweakSubSectionDef.description: Changes the gloomlight often found in mech clusters to produce more light so it's actually useful.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Enabled
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Changes the gloomlight often found in mech clusters to produce more light so it's actually useful.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Work As Sunlamp
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: With Better Gloomlight and this enabled, they'll instead produce enough light to be equal to that of a free sunlamp.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Darklight Glow
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Changes the colour of the gloomlight to match that of 'Darklight'.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Tradeable Meals
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Allows all meals in the "meals" category to be traded with any trader, includes any modded items in that category too.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Trader Pawn Alert
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Shows an alert if there's a trader on the colony map.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Orbital Trader Alert
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Shows an alert if there's an orbital trader, if you have a comms console built.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Don't Generate Relations
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Prevents random relationships from being generated automatically. Will not affect manually created relations through other means.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Disable Lethal Damage Threshold
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Vanilla RimWorld has it so pawns can recieve a maximum of 150 damage across all body parts before killing them. This removes that threshold, so they instead only die from an actual cause.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: hay doesn't need cooling
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Patches hay so it won't rot if it isn't cooled.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: useful grass
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Patches grass and tall grass so when it's cut it provides 2 Hay (less if not fully grown).

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: useful bushes
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Patches bushes so they provide 2 Wood when cut (less if not fully grown).

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Animal Resource Label
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Attaches details to milkable and shearable animals info that tells you how long is left till they can be harvested and what you'll get out of it.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Disable Special Skin Shader
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: In vanilla, skin that isn't overridden to a natural colour by genes has a special shader on it adding a pinkish red tint to it, which personally I think looks horrible on a lot of natural skin tones. This disables it and uses the shader typically assigned when they use an unnatural skin colour.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Boomalopes Bleed Chemfuel
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Changes the blood def from boomalopes and boomrats to be chemfuel puddles instead.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Buildable Packed Dirt
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Simply adds a buildable version of the packed dirt paths from vanilla.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Minifiable Cryptosleep Caskets
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Allows cryptosleep caskets to be moved.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Chatty Comms
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Adds a recreation type to comms consoles allowing them to be used by pawns to gain recreation through 'chatting'.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Destroy Anything
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Allows the smelting of pretty much anything anything in the crematorium aside from weapons, apparel and minified buildings. Be careful so you don't burn anything important.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Disable Narrow Heads
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Removes the narrow head shapes, they do not fit many of even the vanilla hair and beard styles properly and thanks to 1.4 making them defs it is very easy to just YEET. Can cause errors due to mods commonly directly referencing the removed head types.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Don't Pack Food
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Prevents pawns from stuffing food into their inventory to carry around.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Full Deconstruct Return
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Returns the full amount it takes to build something. No more punishment for moving a building that isn't uninstallable.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Glowing Ambrosia
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Gives Ambrosia a slight glow around it, making natural spawning Ambrosia easier to find on a map in the dark.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Glowing Healroot
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Gives Healroot a slight glow around it, making natural spawning Healroot easier to find on a map in the dark.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Growable Ambrosia
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Allows the growing of Ambrosia in plant zones.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Growable Grass
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Allows the growing of grass and tall grass in plant zones. If you have Biotech you can also grow grey grass from that.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Growable Mushrooms
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Allows the growing of Glowstool and Agarilux in plant zones.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Growable Wild Berries
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Allows the growing of wild berries in plant zones.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Healroot to Xerigium
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Reverts the old name change of the herbal medicine plant Healroot back to Xerigium like it used to be in older game versions.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Hidden Wires
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Visually hides the ugly wires that connect to the power conduits from buildings that don't specifically need to be placed on top of conduits.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Incident Pawn Stats
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Displays the information of any pawns rewarded as part of incidents.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Infestation Blocking Floors
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Prevents infestations happening on harder floors (anything crafted from metal or stone materials). Only prevents the event picking that spot, hives can still spawn on them if an event happens closeby.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Insulting Spree Nerf
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description:
Makes the Insulting Spree mental break less annoying to deal with.
- Intensity: Minor to Major
- Max Duration: 45,000 ticks to 20,000 ticks
- Min Duration: 25,000 ticks to 2,500 ticks
- Base Event Chance: 0.5 to 0.15

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Cheaper Hidden Conduits
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: If enabled, changes the cost of hidden conduits to be the same as normal conduits. They already take much longer to build, 2 steel instead of the normal 1 steel on top of that is just rude.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Impassable Deep Water
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Changes deep water to be impassable by pawns, preventing them from pathing through it.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Lag Free Lamps
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Removes the fuel comp from fuelled lamps, so they now no longer run code constantly they impact performance that little bit less.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Lower Prisoner Expectations
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Brings prisoner expectations down to a more reasonable 'low expectations' level. They just tried to kill your colony most of the time, they don't deserve to have expectations.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Megasloth to Megatherium
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Reverts the name change of the Megatherium so it retains the obviously cooler name.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Next Restock Timer
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Displays in the world map information of settlements whether or not they have restocked since you last visited and how long till their next restock.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Sturdier Bridges
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Changes bridge capabilities to handle medium and heavy buildings, now you can build a stone wall over that river raiders keep wandering in through.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Recreational Smokeleaf
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Changes smokeleaf to no longer have a chance of life threatening health conditions, and lowers the debuffs applied by smokeleaf high.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: No Breakdowns
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Removes the breakdown comp from anything that has it, artificially enforced resource sinks are LAZY.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Waterproof Electronics
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Prevents electronics that normally would short circuit in the rain from doing so.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Lower Shell Layering
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Changes the shell layer of all vanilla apparel that as of 1.5 renders over hair when it really should render under it.

TweaksGalore.TweakSubSectionDef.label: No Friend Shaped Manhunters
TweaksGalore.TweakSubSectionDef.description: Sets parameters which decide if an animal can arrive as manhunter or not. This does not prevent it happening if they take damage. This can result in the initial Royalty quest not firing as it requires manhunting animal that specifically fits the parameters this tweak is designed to prevent, I'd recommend enabling this AFTER that quest.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Enabled
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Sets parameters which decide if an animal can arrive as manhunter or not.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Prevent By Trainability
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Controls whether intermediate or advanced trainable animals can be manhunters.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Prevent If Nuzzle-able
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: If animal can nuzzle, it won't spawn as part of manhunter incidents.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Prevent If Wildness Below
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: If the animals wildness is below this value, it won't spawn as part of manhunter incidents.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Prevent If Combat Power Below
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: If the animals combat power is below this value, it won't spawn as part of manhunter incidents.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Prevent When Taming
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Prevents animals that fit the parameters from turning manhunter when taming.

TweaksGalore.TweakSubSectionDef.label: Tainted Apparel
TweaksGalore.TweakSubSectionDef.description: Tweaks specific to tainted apparel.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Disable Taint
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: If enabled, apparel will not be tainted at all, doesn't apply retroactively to existing tainted apparel.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Taint on Rot
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: If enabled, apparel will be tainted when a pawn begins rotting rather than when they die.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Only Taint First Layer
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: If enabled, only apparel covering the innermost layer will be tainted, typically this will result in armour being fine but clothing being tainted.

TweaksGalore.TweakSubSectionDef.label: Prisoners Don't Have Keys
TweaksGalore.TweakSubSectionDef.description: Selectively controls whether prisoners and slaves can open doors during breakout and rebellion.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Enabled
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Selectively controls whether prisoners and slaves can open doors during breakout and rebellion.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Applies to Prisoners
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Whether or not this applies to prisoners.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Applies to Slaves
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Whether or not this applies to slaves.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Can Open Own Door
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Whether or not escaping pawns can open their own door, the one leading into their cell.

TweaksGalore.TweakSubSectionDef.label: Slim Rim
TweaksGalore.TweakSubSectionDef.description: Allows the limiting of pawn body tpes on generation, the replacement will be either Male or Female depending on the pawns current gender.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Enabled
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Allows the limiting of pawn body types on generation, the replacement will be either Male or Female depending on the pawns current gender.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Fat
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: If enabled, limits the fat body type from spawning.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Hulk
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: If enabled, limits the hulk body type from spawning.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Thin
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: If enabled, limits the thin body type from spawning.

TweaksGalore.TweakSubSectionDef.label: Trait Count Adjustment
TweaksGalore.TweakSubSectionDef.description: As of 1.4 this isn't fully functional, changes to the way traits generate made it so the first 1-3 can always generate like normal, regardless of what I do. So this is only usefuly currently for those who want to guarantee more than 1 or have more in general. Won't affect newborns/children as they have a complicated system for their growth.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Enabled
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: If enabled, allows the range to take effect.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Trait Count Range
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Range count of traits which can generate.

TweaksGalore.TweakSubSectionDef.label: Ancient Deconstruction
TweaksGalore.TweakSubSectionDef.description: Makes the Ancient Ruins added by Ideology and/or Biotech deconstructable instead of having to destroy them.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Enabled
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Makes the Ancient Ruins added by Ideology and Biotech deconstructable instead of having to destroy them.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Give Proper Materials
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Changes returned items to some reasonable materials instead of just slag.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Reconstruction
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Makes the Ancient Ruins buildable, using the same materials you would gain from deconstructing them.

TweaksGalore.TweakSubSectionDef.label: Dynamic Population
TweaksGalore.TweakSubSectionDef.description: Provides control over the population thresholds universally, overriding storyteller limitations.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Enabled
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: When enabled, will use the values below to handle population thresholds.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Critically Low
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Population below or equal to this is considered critically low.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Low
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Population below or equal to this is considered low.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Typical
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Population below or equal to this is considered typical.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: High
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Population below or equal to this is considered high.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Critically High
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Population below or equal to this is considered critically high.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Maximum
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Population below or equal to this is considered maximum.

TweaksGalore.TweakSubSectionDef.label: Raid Strategies
TweaksGalore.TweakSubSectionDef.description: Provides control over the raid strategies which can be used by factions. Keep in mind that if a faction only uses strategies you have disabled, they will never be seen, it hasn't come up yet though.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Disable Raiders Fleeing
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: When enabled, will prevent raiders from fleeing.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Disable Breach Raids
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: When enabled, will prevent breach raids.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Disable Drop Pod Raids
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: When enabled, will prevent drop pod raids.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Disable Sapper Raids
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: When enabled, will prevent sapper raids.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Disable Siege Raids
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: When enabled, will prevent siege raids.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Disable Water Raids
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: When enabled, will prevent water raids.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Skilled Stonecutting
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Makes stonecutting give crafting skill increases, and makes more skilled crafters create blocks quicker.

TweaksGalore.TweakSubSectionDef.label: Faster Smoothing
TweaksGalore.TweakSubSectionDef.description: Changes the speed at which stone smoothing is done to a custom value.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Enabled
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Changes the speed at which stone smoothing is done to a custom value.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Speed Factor
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Changes the speed at which stone smoothing is done to a custom value.

TweaksGalore.TweakSubSectionDef.label: Skills
TweaksGalore.TweakSubSectionDef.description: What you statistically speaking, lack.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Enabled
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: If enabled, allows the skill tweaks to function.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Skill Loss Multiplier
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Multiplier on rate of skill loss.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Skill Gain Multiplier
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Multiplier on rate of skill gain.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Skill Loss Threshold
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: The level a skill has to reach before skill loss starts happening, it will prevent skill loss entirely below that level.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Skill Learning Per Day
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: After a set amount of xp has been learnt for this skill since the last midnight passes, the amount that that can be learnt is lowered. This lets you change how much xp a pawn can gain in any given skill before that kicks in.

TweaksGalore.TweakSubSectionDef.label: Hunters Can Use Melee
TweaksGalore.TweakSubSectionDef.description: Allows hunters to use melee, regardless of how well they can do so.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Enabled
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Allows hunters to use melee, regardless of how well they can do so.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Allow Fists
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Allows hunters to use their fists to hunt, stupid but it works.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Mechanoid Heat Armor
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Changes the heat armor mechanoids have, if you leave the setting at the max value (200%, the vanilla default) then it'll be ignored.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Disable Mechanoid Adaptation
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Disables the ability for Mechanoids to adapt to EMP, so EMP remains super effective regardless.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Pre-1.0 Ship Parts
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Returns psychic and defoliator ship parts to their B18 state where they actually provide a decent reward. Psychic Ship Part Leavings: - 100x Steel - 35x Plasteel - 8x Steel Slag - 4x Industrial Components - 1x Spacer Components - 1x AI Persona Core Defoliator Ship Part Leavings: - 100x Steel - 35x Plasteel - 8x Steel Slag - 4x Industrial Component - 1x Spacer Component - 5x Glittertech Medicine

TweaksGalore.TweakSubSectionDef.label: Power Adjusting
TweaksGalore.TweakSubSectionDef.description: If enabled, allows the below power changes to take effect. If they usually produce then it configures how much they output instead, which will instead show as a negative value slider.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Enabled
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: If enabled, allows the below power changes to take effect. Requires restart for the values to actually work, as they're assigned on startup.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Show Tech Level & Counter
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: If enabled, the vanilla research window will now have a small indicator of the tech level of the research project currently selected and have a counter telling you the total projects you have completed for that level.\n\nThis will only ever be applied the the vanilla window, if you want another mods UI to be affected, ask them, there is nothing stopping them implementing their own independant counter!

TweaksGalore.TweakSubSectionDef.label: Tech Traversal
TweaksGalore.TweakSubSectionDef.description: Tweaks specific the players tech level changing as they progress.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Enabled
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: If enabled, allows the rest of the tweaks in the Tech Traversal subsection to function, otherwise they are disabled.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Always Lowest Level
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: If enabled, the players tech level will always be the lowest unfinished tech level. So if you start with the vanilla Crashlanded scenario, instead of starting Ultratech, you'd start Neolithic till you advance through everything.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Lowest Tech Level
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: This allows you to set what the lowest tech level is allowed to be, Neolithic by default as there are no research projects lower than that in vanilla, however I've allowed you to go lower in the case where a mod adds research for that.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Percentage Needed
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: This value dictates how much research of a specific level needs to be completed to move beyond it.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Don't Count Techprints
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: If enabled, this makes the counter and calculation completely ignore any research which requires a techprint.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Only Count Vanilla/DLC Research
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: If enabled, this makes the counter and calculation completely ignore any research added by mods.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Metal Doesn't Burn
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Removes flammability from Steel and Plasteel, setting gold and silver slightly above 0 so they can still 'melt'.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: No Mineable Components
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Removes compacted components from map generation.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: No Mineable Plasteel
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Removes compacted plasteel from map generation.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Old Component Names
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Back in my day we had industrial and spacer components! Now you can too!

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Pretty Precious Metals
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Changes the beauty of gold and silver (the item, not as a material) from -4 to 4.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Stronger Steel
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Doubles the durability of steel as a material.

TweaksGalore.TweakSubSectionDef.label: Stackable Chunks
TweaksGalore.TweakSubSectionDef.description: Allows stone chunks and slag to be stackable. Changing this mid-save WILL cause issues.

TweaksGalore.TweakDef.label: Enabled
TweaksGalore.TweakDef.description: Allows stone chunks and slag to be stackable. Changing this mid-save WILL cause issues.

TweaksGalore.TweakSectionDef.label: Power
TweaksGalore.TweakSectionDef.description: Allows tweaking the usage rate of some buildings.

TweaksGalore.TweakSectionDef.label: Research Projects
TweaksGalore.TweakSectionDef.description: Allows control over the cost and tech print needs of any given Research Project. Restarting the game is required to apply these settings.

TweaksGalore.TweakSectionDef.label: Resources
TweaksGalore.TweakSectionDef.description: This will only function against vanilla versions of the raid types, some modded raids use their own version and will bypass these tweaks.

ThingDef.label: power conduit
ThingDef.description: A burried bundle of electrical cables for moving power around.

HediffDef.label: permanent burn
HediffDef.description: A permanent burn scar that cannot be treated.

HediffDef.label: acid burn
HediffDef.description: A splash of acid that continues to cause burn wounds for quite some time after the initial attack.

HediffDef.label: acid burn
HediffDef.description: An acid burn.
This creature feeds on sunlight. Inadequate levels of light will kill it.
HediffDef.label: level of sunlight

HediffDef.description: Toxins in the bloodstream. This can come from various sources, including environmental toxins, venomous bites, or poisoned weapons. \nAt high doses, toxic buildup is lethal. Even at low doses, it can generate cancers. \nContrary to base game toxic buildup, creatures who die with this toxic damage can be eaten.
HediffDef.label: toxic buildup
hypothermic slowdown
HediffDef.description: Dangerously low core body temperature. Unless re-warmed, hypothermic slowdown gets worse and ends in death. Recovery is quick once the victim is re-warmed.

JobDef.reportString: using TargetA to teleport to TargetB

MentalStateDef.label: xenophobic rage
MentalStateDef.recoveryMessage: {0} is no longer in a xenophobic rage.
MentalStateDef.beginLetter: {0} has flown into a xenophobic rage.\n\n[PAWN_pronoun] has decided to kill {1}.

NeedDef.label: power
NeedDef.description: Power represents the state of a machine's internal battery. If it gets too low, the machine will stop performing tasks and return to its station to recharge.

StatDef.label: ranged weapon cooldown factor
StatDef.description: The cooldown on weapons is multiplied by this value.

StatDef.label: Shield max energy offset

StatDef.label: Shield max energy factor
StatDef.description: Factor of the maximum shield energy that the user can boost through various means.

StatDef.label: shield recharge rate
StatDef.description: The rate at which a shield gains energy as long as it is not broken.

StatDef.label: shield radius
StatDef.description: The area covered when the energy shield is active.

StatDef.label: shield max energy
StatDef.description: The maximum energy a shield generator can have at one time. More energy absorbs more damage.

StatDef.label: shield recharge rate
StatDef.description: The rate at which a shield gains energy as long as it is not broken.

StatDef.label: shield radius

StatDef.label: melee attack speed factor

StatDef.label: range attack speed factor

StatDef.label: melee attack damage factor

StatDef.label: range attack damage factor

StatDef.label: cosmetic body size offset

StatDef.label: cosmetic body size multiplier

StatDef.description: Modifies the pawn's rendered position in y-axis.

StatDef.label: Mass carry capacity
StatDef.description: Total mass carrying capacity of the pawn in caravans.

StatDef.label: MTB Lovin Factor
StatDef.description: A factor of the mean time between (MTB) this person looking for some lovin'.

ThingDef.label: outpost delivery spot
ThingDef.description: Designates a spot for items from outposts to be delivered to.

VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.label: Sharpshooting
VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.description: An expertise in accuracy when firing both high-tech and low-tech ranged weapons.

VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.label: Aiming
VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.description: An expertise in aiming when firing both high-tech and low-tech ranged weapons.

VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.label: Reloading
VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.description: An expertise in reloading both high-tech and low-tech ranged weapons.

VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.label: Piercing
VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.description: An expertise in armor piercing when using sharp melee weapons.

VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.label: Dueling
VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.description: An expertise in the fast-paced armed melee combat.

VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.label: Taming
VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.description: An expertise in taming wild animals.

VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.label: Ranching
VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.description: An expertise in ranching and animal produce gathering.

VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.label: Hunting
VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.description: An expertise in the art of hunting.

VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.label: Handling
VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.description: An expertise in handling and training colony animals.

VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.label: Art Quality
VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.description: An expertise in creating works of art with increased quality.

VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.label: Art Quantity
VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.description: An expertise in creating works of art quickly and efficiently.

VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.label: Flooring
VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.description: An expertise in constructing floors.

VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.label: Repairing
VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.description: An expertise in repairing broken down and damaged structures.

VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.label: Architecture
VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.description: An expertise in creating complex and beautiful buildings.

VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.label: Building
VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.description: An expertise in constructing massive amounts of buildings quickly and efficiently.

VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.label: Butchering
VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.description: An expertise in butchering dead animals.

VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.label: Drug Cooking
VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.description: An expertise in creating drugs.

VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.label: Food Hygiene
VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.description: An expertise in creating safe to consume meals in any environment.

VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.label: Feeding
VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.description: An expertise in creating large amounts of meals to feed many people quickly.

VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.label: Disassembler
VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.description: An expertise in all things mechanoids, including shredding and disassembling them.

VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.label: Tailoring
VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.description: An expertise in tailoring excellent clothes.

VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.label: Weaponsmithing
VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.description: An expertise in creating excellent weapons.

VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.label: Fabricating
VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.description: An expertise in crafting components efficiently.

VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.label: Surgery
VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.description: An expertise in performing safe and effective surgeries.

VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.label: First Aid
VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.description: An expertise at rapid treatment and medical tend speed.

VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.label: Nursing
VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.description: An expertise in caring for ill patients, suffering from various diseases.

VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.label: Drilling
VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.description: An expertise in using a deep drill to mine resources more efficiently.

VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.label: Prospecting
VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.description: An expertise in digging up ore and finding more of it.

VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.label: Tunnelling
VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.description: An expertise in digging massive tunnels and caverns.

VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.label: Geology
VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.description: An expertise in rocks and obtaining more stone chunks when digging.

VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.label: Synthesizing
VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.description: An expertise in creating complex drugs efficiently.

VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.label: Hacking
VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.description: An expertise in hacking terminals and ancient systems.

VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.label: Researching
VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.description: An expertise in researching new technologies.

VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.label: Foraging
VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.description: An expertise in living off the land and foraging the fruits of the forest.

VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.label: Pruning
VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.description: An expertise in communicating psychically and pruning the Gauranlen trees.

VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.label: Harvesting
VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.description: An expertise in ensuring no parts of the plant are wasted on harvesting.

VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.label: Sowing
VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.description: An expertise in quickly sowing and harvesting large amounts of plants.

VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.label: Wardening
VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.description: An expertise in handling prisoners and slaves, recruiting them and arresting them if needed.

VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.label: Negotiating
VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.description: An expertise in handling negotiations and trading.

VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.label: Proselytizing
VSE.Expertise.ExpertiseDef.description: An expertise in converting others to their own ways of thinking.

VSE.Passions.PassionDef.label: natural
VSE.Passions.PassionDef.description: Naturally good at this skill. However, this means they won’t keep up their practice.

VSE.Passions.PassionDef.label: critical
VSE.Passions.PassionDef.description: This skill is extremely important in some way, most likely due to events in their past.

StatDef.description: A multiplier applied to the cooldown of melee attacks by this pawn.

StatDef.label: attack on tame fail chance factor

StatDef.label: art quality bonus
StatDef.description: A bonus to the quality of art produced by this pawn.

StatDef.label: art creation speed
StatDef.description: A multiplier to how fast this pawn creates art.

StatDef.label: roof work speed
StatDef.description: How fast this pawn can work on roofs.

StatDef.label: floor work speed
StatDef.description: How fast this pawn can work on floors.

StatDef.label: repair speed
StatDef.description: How fast this pawn can do repairs.

StatDef.label: construction quality bonus
StatDef.description: A bonus added to the quality of things built by this pawn.

StatDef.label: tailoring speed
StatDef.description: How fast this pawn tailors clothes.

StatDef.label: weapon creation speed
StatDef.description: How fast this pawn can create weapons.

StatDef.label: component crafting speed
StatDef.description: How fast this pawn can create components (both industrial and advanced).

StatDef.label: rock chunk chance
StatDef.description: The chance for this pawn to get a chunk when mining natural rock.

StatDef.label: recruitment rate
StatDef.description: How fast this pawn can recruit prisoners to the colony.

StatDef.description: How likely this pawn is to succeed at peace talks.

IncidentDef.label: wandering caravan arrived
IncidentDef.letterText: Your colonists have spotted a wandering {0} in the distance. The {0} must be a seperated pack animal of another factions trading caravan, as it seems to be carrying containers that look like they could be filled with potentially valuable items. More {0}s may be following close behind.\n\nEither tame or kill it to capture its potentially valuable inventory.

tips.li: The "Equals" key activates the first tool right-click action when something is selected.
Pressing the "Equals" key after selecting a mineable resource will designate the whole cluster for mining.
Some tools in the Orders menu behave differently when used with modifier keys. Hover over the tools for more information.
When something is selected, you can pick up the appropriate tool by holding Shift and clicking one of the command buttons.
Many mods have settings you can tweak to suit your play style. The Mod Settings button is found in the Options menu.
Pressing the "Home" key will allow all forbidden things on the map.
Command buttons with a small mouse icon can be right-clicked for additional special commands.
The "Select similar" tool has many uses. It can help find ore deposits, harvest wild healroot and deconstruct cables under walls.

WorkTypeDef.description: High-priority hauling. Works like the regular kind, but only for things that are manually designated. Use Architect > Orders > Haul Urgently to designate things to haul.\nAdded by the Allow Tool mod. Can be disabled in Options > Mod Settings.
Quickly and painlessly kill downed creatures.\nAdded by the Allow Tool mod. Can be disabled in Options > Mod Settings.

KeyBindingCategoryDef.label: Allow Tool
KeyBindingCategoryDef.description: Shortcuts for designators provided by the Allow Tool mod.

AllowTool.ThingDesignatorDef.label: Allow selection
AllowTool.ThingDesignatorDef.description: Unforbid all items in the selected area. Click and drag over an area to use.

AllowTool.ThingDesignatorDef.label: Forbid selection
AllowTool.ThingDesignatorDef.description: Forbid all items in the selected area. Click and drag over an area to use.

AllowTool.ThingDesignatorDef.label: Allow everything
AllowTool.ThingDesignatorDef.description: Unforbids all forbidden items on the map. Click to activate. Hold Ctrl/Option to include buildings. Hold Shift to include skeletons and non-fresh corpses.

AllowTool.ThingDesignatorDef.label: Select similar
AllowTool.ThingDesignatorDef.description: Selects only things similar to those already selected. Hold Shift to pick additional things. Hold Alt to ignore selection limits.

AllowTool.ThingDesignatorDef.label: Haul urgently
AllowTool.ThingDesignatorDef.description: Mark things to be hauled as soon as possible. Colonists will delay other work until hauling is complete. Configurable in the Work tab. Hold Shift to interrupt current colonist work.

AllowTool.ThingDesignatorDef.label: Finish off
AllowTool.ThingDesignatorDef.description: Quickly and painlessly kill downed creatures. Hold Shift to include colonists and allies.

AllowTool.ThingDesignatorDef.label: Harvest fully grown
AllowTool.ThingDesignatorDef.description: Orders the harvesting or chopping crops and trees that are sufficiently grown to yield their maximum amount of resources when gathered. Hold Shift to include only plants. Hold Ctrl/Option to include only trees.

AllowTool.ThingDesignatorDef.label: Strip mine
AllowTool.ThingDesignatorDef.description: Lays out mine orders in a grid to maximize the chance to find hidden ores. Hold Shift to show settings window or designate using current settings.

HugsLib.UpdateFeatureDef.content: In-game options have been added for hiding unused tools (see Options > Mod Settings).|The Mass Select tool has become a lot more useful. When holding the Control key (Option on Mac), it will select only things of the same type as are already selected. This is great for selecting power conduits under walls, walls made only out of a certain material, all animals of a certain species, and many other things.
The Mass Select tool is now able to select all items or pawns of the same type across the whole map (Hold Alt and click).

Massive update!|New tools:|"Select similar" (formerly Mass select) allows to easily find and select only things similar to those already selected. Great for deconstruction and finding things around the map.|"Haul urgently" allows to have the marked items hauled before any other work is done. Holding Shift will have colonists interrupt current work and begin hauling immediately.|Tool right-click menus:|Tools with the small mouse icon now have a context menu that allows them to affect the whole map. To activate the context menu action for the tool you are holding, you can also press the "Context action" key ("Equals" by default).
New tool:|"Finish off" allows to quickly and humanely clean up downed animals and raid survivors. Requires a colonist skilled in melee combat to carry out the order.

Cut blighted plants: marks all blighted plants on the map to be cut. Right-click the "Cut plants" tool to use.|Cancel all of this type: cancels all designations found on the selected item across the whole map. Useful to undo accidentally issued commands that affect the whole map.

New tools:|Drafted hunt is a tool for manual hunting. When enabled, allows colonists to automatically target and finish off wild animals. Draft a colonist to use, right-click to change settings.|Harvest/Chop fully grown: tools to mark only fully grown plants for harvesting and chopping, which improves resource yield. Right click the "Harvest" or "Chop" tools to use.

Chop tool actions: added "Chop all wood" and "Chop all wood in home area" to the Chop tool's right-click menu.|Pick Up And Haul compatibility: Haul Urgently will now use the custom (and more effective) hauling logic if the Pick Up And Haul mod is installed.

New tools:|Harvest fully grown: Harvesting fully grown things has been promoted to a separate tool, which can now be used in combination with "Select similar". Can selectively mark crops or trees only by holding Shift or Ctrl.|Strip mine: all new tool to easily lay out mining orders in a grid to maximize the chance of finding ores.|Other additions:|Select similar in visible area: added to "Select similar" tool right-click menu.|Customizable tool placement: other mods can now affect where in the menu the tools appear (most notably RIMMSqol).

MoreFactionInteraction.EventDef.label: Game-of-Ur competition
MoreFactionInteraction.EventDef.outComeFirstPlace: Through skill, nerves of steel and a good amount of luck, [PAWN_nameDef] won the tournament! Your reward for participating is:\n\n{0}
MoreFactionInteraction.EventDef.outcomeFirstLoser: For the tense final round, [PAWN_nameDef] went head to head with the five-year reigning champion and lost. Your reward for participating is:\n\n{0}
MoreFactionInteraction.EventDef.outComeFirstOther: During the second inning of the fifth round, [PAWN_nameDef] played a move which confused [PAWN_possessive] opponent and astounded referees. Understandably, a massive brawl ensued. Your reward for participating is:\n\n{0}

MoreFactionInteraction.EventDef.label: Shooting competition
MoreFactionInteraction.EventDef.outComeFirstPlace: With almost robotic accuracy, [PAWN_nameDef] took aim and hit all targets with pinpoint precision. Judges were very impressed and rewarded you with:\n\n{0}
MoreFactionInteraction.EventDef.outcomeFirstLoser: There was a strong field of contenders this year, with many faction representatives having lived as a hunter or just plain decked out in (archotech) bionics. [PAWN_nameDef] stranded somewhere in the quarter finals. Your reward for participating is:\n\n{0}

MoreFactionInteraction.EventDef.label: cultural swap
MoreFactionInteraction.EventDef.themeDesc: There may be an opportunity for trade.
MoreFactionInteraction.EventDef.outComeFirstPlace: As the last of daylight slowly dimmed away, [PAWN_nameDef] simply sat down on a granite stool and told of [PAWN_possessive] upbringing as a [PAWN_title]. This simple story and more importantly the atmosphere [PAWN_pronoun] created was lauded by judges for its intimacy, originality and bravery. Your reward for participating is:\n\n{0}
MoreFactionInteraction.EventDef.outcomeFirstLoser: Not being better prepared or having brought anything, your caravan broke out in a song and dance routine with [PAWN_nameDef] taking centre stage. It wasn't well-rehearsed, which shone through the performance. Not all participating factions were able to appreciate the improvised show, but it was an admirable effort nonetheless. Your reward for participating is:\n\n{0}

MoreFactionInteraction.EventDef.label: Science Fair
MoreFactionInteraction.EventDef.outComeFirstPlace: Settling in easily, a powerful orator and great scholar explains you nothing about the complexities of the universe. Instead they reveal its simplicities:\n\n{0}
MoreFactionInteraction.EventDef.outcomeFirstLoser: Your caravan nestles in between members of a group called "appreciators of science". They bestow upon you a gift of knowledge:\n\n{0}
MoreFactionInteraction.EventDef.outComeFirstOther: Weary from the long journey, your caravan members have trouble staying awake during the long and tenuous lecture by a famous professor. As a departure gift, you get:\n\n{0}

MoreFactionInteraction.EventDef.label: acoustic show
MoreFactionInteraction.EventDef.themeDesc: You wonder whether to bring earplugs.
MoreFactionInteraction.EventDef.outComeFirstPlace: Your caravan spent the day gallivanting through the stalls and admiring the wide array of eclectic non-electric musical instruments from all over this world and beyond. As dusk fell and people gathered their instruments an intimate concert was held on the main-stage. It lifted the spirits of your caravan members. Your reward for coming is:\n\n{0}
MoreFactionInteraction.EventDef.outcomeFirstLoser: The expo turned out to be a very cosy get-together, spent jamming on guitars. Someone played Wonderwall but other than that it was a pretty chill evening that put everybody in a good mood. Your reward for coming is:\n\n{0}
MoreFactionInteraction.EventDef.outComeFirstOther: One of your caravan members picked up an instrument they shouldn't have and, not being musically gifted, broke a string while fingering a minor. Apologies were made but it wasn't sufficient: your klutzy caravan member was to work as a stage-hand on the night of the performance. Since a good time was still had by all, they were given the after-party leftovers:\n\n{0}

IncidentDef.letterText: A group of {0} is passing through the area.\n\nIt's hunting time.

IncidentDef.label: a war is coming?
IncidentDef.letterText:
You've received a message from [PAWN_nameDef], {0} of {1}. Their faction recently had diplomatic troubles with another faction and call upon you to negotiate between them and {2}. They've picked a neutral nearby location and invite you to come negotiate.

It could be a great opportunity to improve relations with their faction, but beware - a poor negotiator can cause more harm than good and even anger them.

The offer will expire after {3} days, after which [PAWN_nameDef] fears the worst.

IncidentDef.label: spreading bandit camp
IncidentDef.letterText: {0}, {1} of {2}, feels the need to sent us a taunting message.\n\nIt states they have set up another outpost.

IncidentDef.label: hunters lodge
IncidentDef.letterText: You are invited to {0}'s {1} summer retreat. {2}. There is an outpost at the site with all the required facilities to make meals, and they've extended their hospitality to you. This offer expires in {3} days.

SitePartDef.arrivedLetter: Your caravan has arrived at the hunter's lodge. It seems nobody is here, but they've obviously been expecting you and have made the place hospitable.

ConceptDef.label: Guest beds
ConceptDef.helpText: Visitors prefer to sleep in beds.\n\nYou can convert beds to guest beds using the "For guests" button.

ConceptDef.label: Recruiting guests
ConceptDef.helpText: You can recruit guests.\n\nRecruiting a guest will cost you goodwill with the guest's faction. Make sure you have a colonist with good social skills assigned for negotiation.

ConceptDef.label: Guests help out
ConceptDef.helpText: Happy guests will help with work inside of their area if they are skilled enough. You can disable this or raise the required skill in the mod options.

ConceptDef.label: Hospitality
ConceptDef.helpText: When a group of visitors arrives, they will use your joy facilities, sleep in guest beds and buy items in their allowed area.\n\nIf they enjoyed their visit, this will increase your reputation with their faction.

ThingDef.Name: LWM_Big_Shelf
ThingDef.label: Big Shelf
ThingDef.description:
A shelf for storing miscellaneous items, from artillery shells to artwork, from bionic arms to bricks, from chairs to corpses. It doesn't ask questions, it just stores things.

Items stored in this will not deteriorate, even if outside.

This shelf holds more than the regular one, and is not limited by weight (use your own judgement).

ThingDef.Name: LWM_VeryBigShelf
ThingDef.label: Very Big Shelves
ThingDef.description:
A set of tall covered shelves for storing miscellaneous items, from artillery shells to artwork, from bionic arms to bricks, from chairs to corpses. It doesn't ask questions, it just stores things.

Pawns access the top shelves using a small rolling ladder (currently not pitured), so while many things can be stored here, it can take a while if you're putting a lot of tiny bottles on the top shelf. Items stored in this will not deteriorate, even if outside.

Note: Use your own judgement about what you put here. Grand Sculptures? Probably don't ACTUALLY fit. But if that's what you want here, you play you! I say go for it!

ThingDef.Name: LWM_MealRack
ThingDef.label: Meal Tray Rack
ThingDef.description: This is a tall tray rack; haulers carry meals and treats here for storage.

ThingDef.Name: LWM_Food_Basket
ThingDef.label: Food Basket
ThingDef.description: A mini-granary for storing raw food and plant matter.

ThingDef.Name: LWM_MeatHook
ThingDef.label: Meat Hook
ThingDef.description:
A tall metal frame with several hooks hanging from chains. A simple crank allows hoisting several hanging things into the air. A way to store the dead bodies of fellow animals you have killed, before cutting them up and consuming their flesh. You monster.
Note that you can only fit so many giant corpses into one space, even if you stack them. The frame will only hold so much weight.

ThingDef.Name: LWM_HayLoft
ThingDef.label: Hayloft
ThingDef.description:
"A hayloft is a space above a barn, stable or cow-shed, traditionally used for storage of hay or other fodder for the animals below. Haylofts were used mainly before the widespread use of industrial sized farm machinery allowed creating very large haybales that cannot be easily lifted for storing..." --Encyclopedia Galactica

Let's be honest here. Unless you're using some farming mods I don't know about, your colonists are probably making piles of hay by hand, which is slow, backbreaking labor. You know what? Most farming is slow, backbreaking labor, and your colonists can't even hire migrant workers from other colonies. Treat farmers and farm workers with respect: they work a lot harder than YOU do ;) Amazing people, good food.

This structure can be used to store hay, silage, and various other plant materials off of damp floors. You probably want to build it under a (very tall) roof.

ThingDef.Name: LWM_FabricHamper
ThingDef.label: Hampers
ThingDef.description: This is a set of hampers made out of fabric. The various pockets allow storing large amounts of diverse small items with ease.\n\nIf you really want to store fabric in bags, see the mod settings!

ThingDef.Name: LWM_Pallet
ThingDef.label: Pallet
ThingDef.description: A flat pallet for packing things. Does not protect against the weather. Sometimes difficult to manage, but useful nonetheless.

ThingDef.Name: LWM_Pallet_Covered
ThingDef.label: Pallet with wrapping
ThingDef.description: A flat pallet for packing things. Wrapping things up in thick oilcloth keeps items secure and organized. You can pack more types of things on this pallet because you can wrap items together, altho this slows you down a little.

ThingDef.Name: LWM_Skip
ThingDef.label: Skip
ThingDef.description:
A large metal bin for tossing heavy things in. These skips are not covered; they are open to the weather.
Note: tossing large amounts of steel in willy-nilly means that it takes a while to find the steel you want later. The mod author has abstracted that as a longer time for storing large stacks of items. Pretend your pawns have to climb in and stack everything so the doggies can pick it up easily.

ThingDef.Name: LWM_Medicine_Cabinet
ThingDef.label: Medicine Cabinet
ThingDef.description: A set of cabinets and shelves for stocking medicines and drugs. Recommended: keep an eye on children.

ThingDef.Name: LWM_Clothing_Rack
ThingDef.label: Clothing Rack
ThingDef.description: A covered rack for storing clothing for easy, quick access and a tidy room.

ThingDef.label: Safe
ThingDef.description: A secure, lockable box for safely storing valuables against theft and/or damage from fire.\n\nNote: protection from fire not yet implemented)

ThingDef.Name: LWM_WeaponsCabinet
ThingDef.label: Weapons Cabinet
ThingDef.description: A sturdy cabinet for storing multiple weapons. Items stored in this will not deteriorate, even if outside.

ThingDef.Name: LWM_WeaponsLocker
ThingDef.label: Weapons Locker
ThingDef.description: A high-capacity metal locker for securely storing many weapons. Items stored in this will not deteriorate, even if outside.

WorkTypeDef.description: Care for the sick, bring them food, cheer them up, and perform assigned duties. Nurses will care for colonists, prisoners and animals.
Perform surgeries on colonists, prisoners and animals.
Rearm defenses such as turrets and traps.
Tame wild animals and train domesticated animals.
Create kibble and butcher meat.
Repair damaged or broken-down buildings and objects.
Uninstall or deconstruct buildings, objects, floors and roofs.
Harvest grown crops.
Use deep drills to drill for resources.
Craft drugs at work stations.
Create weapons and tools from raw materials at a machining table.
Create weapons, armour, bionics and components from raw materials at a fabrication bench.
Refine materials at a refinery.
Perform general production work producing various goods. This typically involves filling and emptying production objects or performing simple tasks.
Operate smelters to perform tasks such as melting down slag or weapons.
Create blocks of stone from rock chunks.
Prepare and unload transport pods, caravans and vehicles.
Perform various tasks relating to dead bodies. Such as operating the crematorium or campfire to burn apparel, drugs and bodies.
Deliver resources to construction projects.
Carry things to where they need to be.
Perform complex work to achieve goals such as finding resources below the ground or in the world.
